rules.rule_name: Session Validation on Program Entry
rules.rule_description: When a user accesses the Transaction Report screen without an active session (no communication area), they must be redirected to the Sign-On screen to authenticate first.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1:Program Entry and Session Validation
Redirect to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Transaction Report screen
acceptance_criteria.When: No active session communication area exists (EIBCALEN = 0), indicating this is the very first call with no prior session context
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and transfers control to the previous screen navigation routine, preventing unauthorized access to the report screen

rules.rule_name: Load Existing Session Communication Area
rules.rule_description: When a user accesses the Transaction Report screen with an active session, the system restores the existing session context from the communication area to maintain continuity.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1:Program Entry and Session Validation
Load Existing Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user navigates to the Transaction Report screen
acceptance_criteria.When: An active session communication area exists (EIBCALEN is greater than 0)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system loads the full contents of the communication area (DFHCOMMAREA) into the working session data area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) to restore the user's session context

rules.rule_name: Initial Transaction Report Screen Display
rules.rule_description: On the first visit to the Transaction Report screen within a session, the screen is presented in a clean state with all fields blank and the cursor positioned on the Monthly report option to guide the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2:Initial Screen Display
Initialize Screen with Blank Fields
Set Cursor to Monthly Option

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has an active session and navigates to the Transaction Report screen for the first time (program re-entry flag is not set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects this is not a re-entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is false)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the re-entry flag to TRUE, initializes the output screen map (CORPT0AO) to LOW-VALUES (blank), positions the cursor on the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), and sends the Transaction Report screen with an erase command to display a clean screen

rules.rule_name: Receive User Input from Transaction Report Screen
rules.rule_description: On subsequent visits (re-entries), the system retrieves all user-entered data from the Transaction Report screen before processing any actions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3:Screen Input Reception
Receive User Inputs from
Transaction Report Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has previously been presented the Transaction Report screen and has entered data or pressed a key
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects this is a re-entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is true)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system receives the screen input from map CORPT0A in mapset CORPT00 into the input data area (CORPT0AI), capturing all user-entered field values for subsequent processing

rules.rule_name: Invalid Key Press Handling
rules.rule_description: If the user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3, the system rejects the action and informs the user that the key pressed is not valid for this screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:User Key Action Handling
Display Invalid Key Error
Redisplay Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen and has received the screen input
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER (DFHENTER) or PF3 (DFHPF3)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', positions the cursor on the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), sets the error message to the invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) stored in WS-MESSAGE, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_name: Navigate Back to Main Menu via PF3
rules.rule_description: Pressing PF3 on the Transaction Report screen returns the user to the Main Menu screen, allowing them to exit without submitting a report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:User Key Action Handling
Navigate Back to Main Menu
COMEN01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key (DFHPF3)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Main Menu (COMEN01C) and performs the return-to-previous-screen routine, transferring control to the Main Menu with the current communication area

rules.rule_name: Report Type Selection Requirement
rules.rule_description: The user must select one of the available report types (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom) before the system can proceed with report submission. Pressing ENTER without a selection is not permitted.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5:Report Type Selection Validation
Display Error: Select a Report Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen and presses the ENTER key
acceptance_criteria.When: None of the report type fields are selected — Monthly (MONTHLYI), Yearly (YEARLYI), and Custom (CUSTOMI) are all spaces or LOW-VALUES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Select a report type to print report...', positions the cursor on the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_name: Monthly Report Start Date Calculation
rules.rule_description: When the Monthly report type is selected, the system automatically determines the start date as the first day of the current calendar month, eliminating the need for manual date entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6:Monthly Report Date Calculation
Calculate First Day of Current Month
as Start Date

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Monthly report type (MONTHLYI is not spaces or LOW-VALUES) and pressed ENTER
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the Monthly report selection
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current date, sets the report name to 'Monthly', assigns the current year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) to WS-START-DATE-YYYY, assigns the current month (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) to WS-START-DATE-MM, assigns '01' to WS-START-DATE-DD, and copies WS-START-DATE to both PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2

rules.rule_name: Monthly Report End Date Calculation
rules.rule_description: When the Monthly report type is selected, the system automatically calculates the last day of the current calendar month as the end date, correctly handling month-end boundaries and year rollovers.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6:Monthly Report Date Calculation
Calculate Last Day of Current Month
as End Date

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Monthly report start date has been set to the first day of the current month
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the end date for the Monthly report
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the day to 1, adds 1 to the current month; if the resulting month exceeds 12, it increments the year by 1 and resets the month to 1; then computes the end date as one day before the first day of the next month using DATE-OF-INTEGER and INTEGER-OF-DATE functions; assigns the resulting year, month, and day to WS-END-DATE-YYYY, WS-END-DATE-MM, and WS-END-DATE-DD respectively; and copies WS-END-DATE to both PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2

rules.rule_name: Yearly Report Start Date Calculation
rules.rule_description: When the Yearly report type is selected, the system automatically sets the start date to January 1st of the current year.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7:Yearly Report Date Calculation
Set Start Date to Jan 1st
of Current Year

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type (YEARLYI is not spaces or LOW-VALUES) and pressed ENTER
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the Yearly report selection
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current date, sets the report name to 'Yearly', assigns the current year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) to WS-START-DATE-YYYY, assigns '01' to WS-START-DATE-MM, assigns '01' to WS-START-DATE-DD, and copies WS-START-DATE to both PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2

rules.rule_name: Yearly Report End Date Calculation
rules.rule_description: When the Yearly report type is selected, the system automatically sets the end date to December 31st of the current year.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7:Yearly Report Date Calculation
Set End Date to Dec 31st
of Current Year

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Yearly report start date has been set to January 1st of the current year
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the end date for the Yearly report
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system assigns the current year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) to WS-END-DATE-YYYY, assigns '12' to WS-END-DATE-MM, assigns '31' to WS-END-DATE-DD, and copies WS-END-DATE to both PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2

rules.rule_name: Custom Date Range - Start Month Empty Validation
rules.rule_description: When the Custom report type is selected, the Start Date Month field is mandatory and must not be left blank.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8:Custom Date Range - Empty Field Validation
Validate All Six Date Fields
Are Not Empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type (CUSTOMI is not spaces or LOW-VALUES) and pressed ENTER
acceptance_criteria.When: The Start Date Month field (SDTMMI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Month can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the Start Month field (SDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_name: Custom Date Range - Start Day Empty Validation
rules.rule_description: When the Custom report type is selected, the Start Date Day field is mandatory and must not be left blank.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8:Custom Date Range - Empty Field Validation
Validate All Six Date Fields
Are Not Empty

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and the Start Date Month field has been provided
acceptance_criteria.When: The Start Date Day field (SDTDDI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Day can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the Start Day field (SDTDDL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_description: When the Custom report type is selected, the Start Date Year field is mandatory and must not be left blank.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and both Start Date Month and Day fields have been provided

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Year can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the Start Year field (SDTYYYYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all three Start Date fields have been provided
acceptance_criteria.When: The End Date Month field (EDTMMI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Month can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the End Month field (EDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Day can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the End Day field (EDTDDL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all five other date fields have been provided

rules.rule_name: Custom Date Range - Numeric Conversion of Date Fields
rules.rule_description: After confirming all six custom date fields are non-empty, the system converts each field to its numeric equivalent to prepare for range and validity checks.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9:Custom Date Range - Numeric Field Validation
Convert and Validate All Date Fields
Contain Valid Numeric Values

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all six date fields (SDTMMI, SDTDDI, SDTYYYYI, EDTMMI, EDTDDI, EDTYYYYI) are non-empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to numeric validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system uses NUMVAL-C function to convert each of the six date fields to their numeric values: Start Month and End Month are stored as 2-digit numbers (WS-NUM-99), Start Day and End Day are stored as 2-digit numbers (WS-NUM-99), and Start Year and End Year are stored as 4-digit numbers (WS-NUM-9999); the converted values are moved back into their respective input fields

rules.rule_name: Custom Date Range - Start Month Range Validation
rules.rule_description: The Start Date Month entered for a Custom report must be a valid numeric month value between 1 and 12.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

Validate Month Not Greater Than 12
Day Not Greater Than 31

acceptance_criteria.When: The Start Date Month (SDTMMI of CORPT0AI) is not numeric OR its value is greater than '12'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Not a valid Month...', positions the cursor on the Start Month field (SDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_name: Custom Date Range - Start Day Range Validation

rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.When: The Start Date Day (SDTDDI of CORPT0AI) is not numeric OR its value is greater than '31'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Not a valid Day...', positions the cursor on the Start Day field (SDTDDL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

acceptance_criteria.When: The Start Date Year (SDTYYYYI of CORPT0AI) is not numeric
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Not a valid Year...', positions the cursor on the Start Year field (SDTYYYYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_name: Custom Start Date Calendar Validity Check
rules.rule_description: After numeric and range validations pass, the custom Start Date must represent a real calendar date (e.g., February 30 is not a valid calendar date). An external date validation service is invoked to confirm this.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11:Custom Start Date - Calendar Validity Check
Call CSUTLDTC to Validate
Start Date is Real Calendar Date

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a Custom report date range and all numeric and range validations have passed for the Start Date fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The system assembles the Start Date from SDTYYYYI, SDTMMI, and SDTDDI into WS-START-DATE and calls the external date validation program CSUTLDTC with the date and date format (WS-DATE-FORMAT)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the validation result severity code (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD) is '0000', the Start Date is valid and processing continues; if the severity code is not '0000' AND the message number (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM) is not '2513', the system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Not a valid date...', positions the cursor on the Start Month field (SDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_name: Custom End Date Calendar Validity Check
rules.rule_description: After the Start Date is validated as a real calendar date, the custom End Date must also represent a real calendar date. An external date validation service is invoked to confirm this.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12:Custom End Date - Calendar Validity Check
Call CSUTLDTC to Validate
End Date is Real Calendar Date

acceptance_criteria.Given: The custom Start Date has passed calendar validity and the End Date fields (EDTYYYYI, EDTMMI, EDTDDI) have passed numeric and range validations
acceptance_criteria.When: The system assembles the End Date from EDTYYYYI, EDTMMI, and EDTDDI into WS-END-DATE and calls the external date validation program CSUTLDTC with the date and date format (WS-DATE-FORMAT)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the validation result severity code (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD) is '0000', the End Date is valid and processing continues; if the severity code is not '0000' AND the message number (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM) is not '2513', the system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Not a valid date...', positions the cursor on the End Month field (EDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_name: Report Print Confirmation Prompt
rules.rule_description: Before submitting any report job for printing, the system requires the user to explicitly confirm the action by entering a value in the confirmation field. An empty confirmation field triggers a prompt.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13:Report Submission Confirmation Request
Prompt User to Confirm Printing
of Selected Report Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: A report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom) has been selected and all date validations have passed
acceptance_criteria.When: The Confirmation field (CONFIRMI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES (left empty by the user)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', constructs the message 'Please confirm to print the [WS-REPORT-NAME] report...' using the selected report name, positions the cursor on the Confirmation field (CONFIRML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen awaiting user confirmation

rules.rule_name: Report Submission Cancellation via Confirmation
rules.rule_description: If the user enters 'N' or 'n' in the confirmation field, the report submission is cancelled, all input fields are cleared, and the screen is refreshed for a new selection.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14:Confirmation Value Validation
Cancel Request
Clear All Fields and Redisplay

acceptance_criteria.Given: A report type has been selected, all validations have passed, and the user has entered a value in the Confirmation field
acceptance_criteria.When: The Confirmation field (CONFIRMI of CORPT0AI) contains 'N' or 'n'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system performs the initialize-all-fields routine which resets all screen input fields (MONTHLYI, YEARLYI, CUSTOMI, SDTMMI, SDTDDI, SDTYYYYI, EDTMMI, EDTDDI, EDTYYYYI, CONFIRMI, WS-MESSAGE) to their initial empty state, sets the cursor to the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), sets the error flag to 'Y', and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_name: Invalid Confirmation Value Rejection
rules.rule_description: The confirmation field only accepts 'Y', 'y', 'N', or 'n'. Any other value entered is rejected with an informative error message showing the invalid value entered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14:Confirmation Value Validation
Display Error: Not a Valid
Confirmation Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: A report type has been selected, all validations have passed, and the user has entered a value in the Confirmation field
acceptance_criteria.When: The Confirmation field (CONFIRMI of CORPT0AI) contains any value other than 'Y', 'y', 'N', or 'n'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', constructs the error message by concatenating '"', the entered confirmation value (CONFIRMI), and '" is not a valid value to confirm...' into WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the Confirmation field (CONFIRML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_name: Batch Job JCL Preparation with Date Parameters
rules.rule_description: Once the user confirms the report submission, the system prepares the batch job by embedding the calculated or entered start and end dates into the job parameters before submission.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15:Batch Job JCL Construction
Prepare JCL Records with
Start and End Dates Embedded

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has confirmed the report submission with 'Y' or 'y' and no errors exist
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the batch job for submission
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies WS-START-DATE to both PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2, and copies WS-END-DATE to both PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2, embedding the date range parameters into the JCL job records (JOB-LINES) that will be submitted

rules.rule_name: Batch Job Submission to Internal Reader
rules.rule_description: The prepared batch report job is submitted for execution by writing JCL records sequentially to the JOBS internal reader queue. The process continues until all records are written or an end-of-file marker is encountered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16:Batch Job Submission to Internal Reader
Write JCL Records Line-by-Line
to JOBS Transient Data Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has confirmed the report submission and the JCL records have been prepared with the correct date parameters
acceptance_criteria.When: The system iterates through JOB-LINES records from index 1 up to a maximum of 1000 records, writing each JCL-RECORD to the JOBS transient data queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: Each record is written to the JOBS queue; the loop terminates when a record equals '/*EOF' or is spaces or LOW-VALUES; if all records are written successfully, processing continues to the success notification; if any write operation fails, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Unable to Write TDQ (JOBS)...', positions the cursor on the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

rules.rule_name: Successful Report Job Submission Notification
rules.rule_description: After a report job is successfully submitted to the print queue with no errors, the user receives a clear visual confirmation in green text, and all input fields are reset for a potential new submission.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
17:Job Submission Success Notification
Clear All Input Fields
Set Message Color to Green
Display Success Confirmation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The report job has been successfully written to the JOBS queue and no error flag is set (ERR-FLG-ON is false)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the job submission process without any errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system performs the initialize-all-fields routine to reset all screen input fields, sets the error message color to green (DFHGREEN) for ERRMSGC of CORPT0AO, constructs the success message by concatenating WS-REPORT-NAME (delimited by space) with ' report submitted for printing ...' into WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen with the green success message

rules.rule_name: Screen Header Population with Current Date and Time
rules.rule_description: Every time the Transaction Report screen is displayed, the header section is refreshed with current system information including the application titles, transaction identifier, program name, and the current date and time.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
18:Screen Header Population
Populate Header with Title, Transaction ID,
Program Name, Date and Time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Report screen is about to be sent to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the populate-header-info routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current date and time, populates the screen header with: application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01 to TITLE01O), application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02 to TITLE02O), transaction name (WS-TRANID to TRNNAMEO), program name (WS-PGMNAME to PGMNAMEO), current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY to CURDATEO), and current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS to CURTIMEO)

rules.rule_name: All Screen Input Fields Initialization
rules.rule_description: When a reset is required (after successful submission or cancellation), all screen input fields are cleared to their initial empty state and the cursor is repositioned to the Monthly report option field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
19:All Fields Initialization
Reset All Screen Input Fields
Set Cursor to Monthly Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: A report submission has been successfully completed or the user has cancelled the submission with 'N'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs the initialize-all-fields routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the cursor position to the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1) and initializes (clears to empty/default) all input fields: MONTHLYI, YEARLYI, CUSTOMI, SDTMMI, SDTDDI, SDTYYYYI, EDTMMI, EDTDDI, EDTYYYYI, CONFIRMI, and WS-MESSAGE

rules.rule_name: Navigation to Previous Screen
rules.rule_description: When navigating away from the Transaction Report screen, the system transfers control to the designated target program while preserving the session communication area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
20:Navigation to Previous Screen
Transfer Control Back to
Main Menu with Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system needs to navigate away from the Transaction Report screen (either due to no active session or PF3 key press)
acceptance_criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen routine is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is LOW-VALUES or spaces, it defaults to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C); the system then sets CDEMO-FROM-TRANID to WS-TRANID, sets CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM to WS-PGMNAME, sets CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT to zeros, and transfers control to CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM via XCTL passing the CARDDEMO-COMMAREA

rules.rule_name: Detect First-Time Program Call with No Active Session
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the user has an active session when entering the Transaction Report program. If no session communication area exists, the user has not yet authenticated and must be redirected.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this the First Time the Program is Called? No Session Exists?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Transaction Report screen
acceptance_criteria.When: No active session communication area exists (session length equals zero), indicating the user has not yet signed on
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a first-time call with no valid session and initiates a redirect to the Sign-On screen

rules.rule_name: Set Default Destination to Sign-On Screen on First Call
rules.rule_description: When no active session exists, the system explicitly sets the navigation destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) so the user can authenticate before accessing the report functionality.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Destination to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that no active session exists (first-time program call)
acceptance_criteria.When: The destination screen needs to be assigned for the redirect
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination program is set to the Sign-On screen identifier 'COSGN00C'

rules.rule_name: Validate That a Destination Screen Has Been Assigned
rules.rule_description: Before redirecting the user, the system verifies that a valid destination screen has been assigned. This prevents navigation failures caused by an unset or blank destination program identifier.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Destination Screen Valid?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to redirect the user away from the Transaction Report screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The destination program identifier is checked for validity
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the destination program identifier is empty or contains only low-values (uninitialized), the destination is considered not set and a default must be applied; if the destination is already set to a valid value, the system proceeds with that destination

rules.rule_name: Apply Default Sign-On Screen When Destination Is Not Set
rules.rule_description: If the destination screen identifier has not been assigned or is blank, the system defaults the navigation target to the Sign-On screen to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default Destination to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to redirect the user and the destination program identifier is either empty or contains only low-values (uninitialized)
acceptance_criteria.When: The destination validation check finds no valid destination has been set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The destination program is defaulted to the Sign-On screen identifier 'COSGN00C'

rules.rule_name: Record Current Transaction and Program Name for Return Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring the user to another screen, the system records the current transaction identifier, program name, and resets the program context. This navigation breadcrumb allows the destination screen to know where the user came from and enables correct return navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Transaction and Program Name for Return Navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to redirect the user to another screen (Sign-On or other destination)
acceptance_criteria.When: Navigation context is being prepared prior to the screen transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction identifier is saved as the originating transaction, the current program name is saved as the originating program, and the program context counter is reset to zero

rules.rule_name: Redirect User to Destination Screen
rules.rule_description: The system transfers control to the designated destination screen, passing the current session data. This ends the current program's execution and hands control entirely to the destination program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redirect User to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination screen has been validated and set, and the navigation context (originating transaction and program) has been recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the screen transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program (Sign-On screen 'COSGN00C' or other valid destination) with the current session communication area passed along, and the Transaction Report program terminates its current execution

rules.rule_name: Load Existing Session Data for Processing
rules.rule_description: When an active user session exists, the system retrieves and loads the session communication area data that was passed from the previous screen. This session data contains user context, navigation history, and program state needed for processing the report request.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Load Existing Session Data for Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user accesses the Transaction Report screen and an active session communication area exists (session length is greater than zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms a valid session is present
acceptance_criteria.Then: The full session communication area data is loaded into the working session data area for use throughout the current program execution, using the exact length of the passed communication area

rules.rule_name: Detect First Entry and Trigger Initial Screen Setup
rules.rule_description: The program determines whether the current interaction is the first entry (not a re-entry) by checking the program re-entry flag. If it is the first entry, the initial screen setup sequence is triggered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Start: First Entry into Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has navigated to the Transaction Report Request screen and the program communication area is available (session is active)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is NOT set to TRUE, indicating this is the first time the user has entered this screen in the current session
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program proceeds to execute the initial screen display sequence: marking the session as re-entry, clearing screen fields, setting cursor focus, and displaying the screen

rules.rule_name: Mark Session as Re-Entry for Subsequent Interactions
rules.rule_description: Immediately upon first entry, the program marks the session state as a re-entry so that any subsequent return to this screen (e.g., after pressing ENTER) is correctly identified as a re-entry and processed accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Program as Re-Entry
for Next Interaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has confirmed this is the first entry into the Transaction Report Request screen (re-entry flag is not set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The initial screen setup sequence begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to TRUE so that the next interaction with this screen is recognized as a re-entry and the user's input is processed rather than the screen being re-initialized

rules.rule_name: Initialize All Transaction Report Screen Fields to Blank
rules.rule_description: On first entry, all output fields on the Transaction Report screen are cleared to blank (LOW-VALUES) to ensure the user is presented with a clean, empty form with no residual data from any prior session or navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Initialize All Screen Fields
to Blank Values

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has confirmed this is the first entry into the Transaction Report Request screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen initialization sequence is executing
acceptance_criteria.Then: All fields in the Transaction Report output screen area (CORPT0AO) are set to LOW-VALUES (blank), ensuring no previously displayed data, messages, or field values are visible to the user

rules.rule_name: Set Cursor Focus to Monthly Report Option Field
rules.rule_description: When the Transaction Report screen is first displayed, the cursor is automatically positioned on the Monthly report option field, guiding the user to begin their selection from the first available report type option.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Cursor Focus
to Monthly Report Option

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Report screen is being prepared for its initial display to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen is about to be sent to the user's terminal for the first time
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor is positioned on the Monthly report option input field (MONTHLYL of CORPT0AI is set to -1), so the user's focus is directed to the first report type selection option

rules.rule_name: Display the Transaction Report Request Screen to the User
rules.rule_description: After all screen fields have been initialized and cursor focus has been set, the Transaction Report Request screen is sent to the user's terminal with the erase option active, fully replacing any previously displayed content, and the system awaits the user's input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Transaction
Report Request Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: All screen fields have been initialized to blank values and the cursor has been positioned on the Monthly report option field
acceptance_criteria.When: The SEND-TRNRPT-SCREEN procedure is performed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Report Request screen (MAP: CORPT0A, MAPSET: CORPT00) is displayed to the user with the ERASE option active (clearing the entire terminal screen before display), the header is populated with the current system date and time, and the system returns control to CICS awaiting the user's next interaction

rules.rule_name: Receive Transaction Report Screen on Re-Entry
rules.rule_description: The system receives and captures all user inputs from the transaction report screen only when the user is returning to the screen (re-entry), not on the initial display. This ensures that user-entered data is only processed after the screen has been presented to the user at least once.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User Submits Transaction Report Request Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has previously been presented with the Transaction Report Request screen and the session communication area indicates the program has been re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the Transaction Report Request screen by pressing a key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system receives and captures all user inputs from the Transaction Report screen (CORPT0A in mapset CORPT00) into the input map area (CORPT0AI), making all entered field values available for subsequent processing

rules.rule_name: Capture Report Type Selection Field
rules.rule_description: The system identifies the user's chosen report type by evaluating which of the three report type indicator fields — Monthly, Yearly, or Custom — contains a non-blank, non-empty value. Only one report type should be selected at a time, and the first non-empty field encountered determines the report type to be processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Report Type Selection Monthly / Yearly / Custom

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Report Request screen and all screen inputs have been received into the input map area (CORPT0AI)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the report type selection fields in the order: Monthly (MONTHLYI), then Yearly (YEARLYI), then Custom (CUSTOMI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The report type is determined as follows: if MONTHLYI is not spaces and not empty, the report type is 'Monthly'; else if YEARLYI is not spaces and not empty, the report type is 'Yearly'; else if CUSTOMI is not spaces and not empty, the report type is 'Custom'; if none of the three fields contain a value, no report type is selected and the system will require the user to make a selection

rules.rule_name: Capture Custom Report Start Date Fields
rules.rule_description: When the Custom report type is selected, the system captures the three individual components of the custom start date entered by the user: the start month, start day, and start year. These are captured as separate fields and will be subject to individual validation before being assembled into a complete start date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Custom Date Range Fields Start Month, Start Day, Start Year

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Report Request screen with the Custom report type selected (CUSTOMI is not spaces and not empty) and has entered values in the custom date range fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the custom date range inputs from the received screen data (CORPT0AI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures the following start date component fields from the screen input: Start Month (SDTMMI of CORPT0AI), Start Day (SDTDDI of CORPT0AI), and Start Year (SDTYYYYI of CORPT0AI), making each field individually available for validation and date assembly

rules.rule_name: Capture Custom Report End Date Fields
rules.rule_description: When the Custom report type is selected, the system captures the three individual components of the custom end date entered by the user: the end month, end day, and end year. These are captured as separate fields and will be subject to individual validation before being assembled into a complete end date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Custom Date Range Fields End Month, End Day, End Year

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Report Request screen with the Custom report type selected (CUSTOMI is not spaces and not empty) and has entered values in the custom date range fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the custom date range inputs from the received screen data (CORPT0AI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures the following end date component fields from the screen input: End Month (EDTMMI of CORPT0AI), End Day (EDTDDI of CORPT0AI), and End Year (EDTYYYYI of CORPT0AI), making each field individually available for validation and date assembly

rules.rule_name: Capture Print Confirmation Field
rules.rule_description: The system captures the user's confirmation response from the screen. This confirmation field is required before any report job is submitted for printing, and its value determines whether the report submission proceeds, is cancelled, or results in a validation error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Confirmation Field Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Report Request screen and all screen inputs have been received into the input map area (CORPT0AI)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the received screen inputs
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures the value entered in the Confirmation field (CONFIRMI of CORPT0AI), making it available for subsequent confirmation validation; the field value may be 'Y', 'y', 'N', 'n', blank/empty, or any other entered value

rules.rule_name: Route Captured Inputs for Further Processing Based on Key Pressed
rules.rule_description: After all screen inputs are captured, the system routes the processing based on which key the user pressed. Only the ENTER key triggers report processing; PF3 navigates back to the main menu; any other key results in an invalid key error. This routing ensures all captured inputs are directed to the correct processing path.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Pass All Captured Inputs for Further Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Report Request screen and all inputs including report type selection, custom date range fields, and confirmation field have been captured from the screen (CORPT0AI)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the key pressed by the user (EIBAID)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes processing as follows: if the ENTER key (DFHENTER) was pressed, all captured inputs are passed to the Enter Key Processing function (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY) for report type evaluation, date validation, and job submission; if PF3 (DFHPF3) was pressed, the user is navigated to the Main Menu screen (COMEN01C) and captured inputs are not processed further; if any other key was pressed, an error message 'Invalid Key' (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) is displayed, the error flag is set to 'Y', the cursor is repositioned to the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), and the screen is redisplayed without processing the captured inputs

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture All User Inputs from Report Request Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has previously been presented with the Transaction Report Request screen and has entered data into one or more fields (report type selection, date fields, confirmation field)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen by pressing any key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures and reads all user-entered input data from the Transaction Report Request screen (CORPT0A / CORPT00) into the working input area (CORPT0AI) so that the data is available for subsequent key evaluation and business processing

rules.rule_name: Route to Report Processing When ENTER Key Is Pressed
rules.rule_description: When the user presses the ENTER key on the Transaction Report Request screen, the system must route the request to the report validation and submission process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Process the Report Request
Validate and Submit Report

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered data on the Transaction Report Request screen and all user inputs have been captured from the screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the key pressed and determines it is the ENTER key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system invokes the report request processing routine (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY) to validate the selected report type, date range inputs, and proceed with report submission

rules.rule_name: Navigate Back to Main Menu When PF3 Key Is Pressed
rules.rule_description: When the user presses the PF3 key on the Transaction Report Request screen, the system must set the navigation destination to the Main Menu and transfer control to it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Destination to
Main Menu - COMEN01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report Request screen and all user inputs have been captured
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the key pressed and determines it is the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Main Menu (COMEN01C) and transfers control to the Main Menu screen, passing along the current session communication area

rules.rule_name: Display Invalid Key Error Message for Unrecognized Key Press
rules.rule_description: When the user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3 on the Transaction Report Request screen, the system must flag an error, display an invalid key message, and redisplay the screen with the cursor repositioned to the Monthly report field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Invalid Key
Error Flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report Request screen and all user inputs have been captured
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the key pressed and determines it is neither the ENTER key nor the PF3 key (i.e., any other function key or action key)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active ('Y'), positions the cursor on the Monthly report selection field, populates the screen error message area with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the Transaction Report Request screen to the user awaiting the next valid key action

rules.rule_name: Monthly Report Type Selection and Routing
rules.rule_description: When the user selects the Monthly report type on the Transaction Report screen, the system recognizes the selection and routes processing to the Monthly report workflow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Monthly Report Type Selected?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen and has pressed the ENTER key
acceptance_criteria.When: The Monthly report type field (MONTHLYI) contains a non-blank, non-empty value indicating the user has selected the Monthly report option
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the report name to 'Monthly' and proceeds to the Monthly Report processing workflow to calculate date ranges and prepare the report for submission

rules.rule_name: Yearly Report Type Selection and Routing
rules.rule_description: When the Monthly report type is not selected but the Yearly report type is selected on the Transaction Report screen, the system recognizes the selection and routes processing to the Yearly report workflow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Yearly Report Type Selected?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen, has pressed the ENTER key, and the Monthly report type field is blank or empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The Yearly report type field (YEARLYI) contains a non-blank, non-empty value indicating the user has selected the Yearly report option
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the report name to 'Yearly' and proceeds to the Yearly Report processing workflow to calculate date ranges and prepare the report for submission

rules.rule_name: Custom Report Type Selection and Routing
rules.rule_description: When neither Monthly nor Yearly report types are selected but the Custom report type is selected on the Transaction Report screen, the system recognizes the selection and routes processing to the Custom report workflow requiring user-entered date ranges.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Custom Report Type Selected?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen, has pressed the ENTER key, and both the Monthly and Yearly report type fields are blank or empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The Custom report type field (CUSTOMI) contains a non-blank, non-empty value indicating the user has selected the Custom report option
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the report name to 'Custom' and proceeds to the Custom Report processing workflow, which requires the user to provide a valid start date and end date for the report range

rules.rule_name: No Report Type Selected — Mandatory Selection Validation
rules.rule_description: When the user presses ENTER without selecting any report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), the system enforces that a report type selection is mandatory before any report can be submitted.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
No Report Type Selected
Set Error Flag

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen and has pressed the ENTER key
acceptance_criteria.When: None of the three report type fields — Monthly (MONTHLYI), Yearly (YEARLYI), or Custom (CUSTOMI) — contain a non-blank, non-empty value, meaning no report type has been selected
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Select a report type to print report...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Monthly report type field to guide the user, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen with the error message visible

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Current System Date for Monthly Report
rules.rule_description: When the Monthly report type is selected, the system must retrieve the current system date to use as the basis for calculating the report's start and end dates.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Current System Date
Year, Month, Day

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Monthly report type on the Transaction Report screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins calculating the date range for the Monthly report
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date, capturing the current Year, current Month, and current Day as the basis for all subsequent date calculations

rules.rule_name: Set Monthly Report Start Date to First Day of Current Month
rules.rule_description: The start date for the Monthly report is automatically determined as the first day of the current calendar month, using the current system year and month.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Start Date
Year = Current Year
Month = Current Month
Day = 01
First Day of Current Month

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has retrieved the current system date with Year, Month, and Day components
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the start date for the Monthly report
acceptance_criteria.Then: The start date is set with Year equal to the current system year, Month equal to the current system month, and Day fixed to '01', representing the first day of the current month

rules.rule_name: Advance to First Day of Next Month for End Date Calculation
rules.rule_description: To determine the last day of the current month, the system first calculates the first day of the next month by advancing the month by 1 and setting the day to 1.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Calculate End Date
Advance Month by 1
Set Day = 1
First Day of Next Month

acceptance_criteria.Given: The start date for the Monthly report has been set to the first day of the current month
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the intermediate date needed to derive the end date
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the day component to 1 and increments the month component by 1, producing the first day of the next month as an intermediate calculation value

rules.rule_name: Handle December to January Year Rollover for Monthly Report End Date
rules.rule_description: When the current month is December, advancing the month by 1 would produce month 13, which is invalid. The system must roll over to January of the next year.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Advanced
Month Greater
Than 12?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has advanced the month by 1 as part of the Monthly report end date calculation
acceptance_criteria.When: The advanced month value is greater than 12 (i.e., the current month is December)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system increments the year by 1 and resets the month to 1 (January), so that the intermediate date correctly represents January 1st of the following year

rules.rule_name: Calculate Last Day of Current Month by Subtracting One Day
rules.rule_description: The last day of the current month is derived by subtracting exactly one day from the first day of the next month, correctly handling all month-length variations including leap years.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Calculate Last Day of Current Month
Subtract 1 Day from
First Day of Next Month

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined the first day of the next month (with year rollover applied if necessary)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the last day of the current month
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system converts the first day of next month to an integer date representation, subtracts 1, and converts back to a calendar date, yielding the correct last day of the current month including proper handling of months with 28, 29, 30, or 31 days

rules.rule_name: Set Monthly Report End Date from Calculated Last Day
rules.rule_description: After computing the last day of the current month, the system assigns the resulting year, month, and day components to form the end date of the Monthly report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set End Date
Year, Month, Day
from Calculated Last Day

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has calculated the last day of the current month
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the end date for the Monthly report
acceptance_criteria.Then: The end date Year is set to the year component of the calculated last day, the end date Month is set to the month component of the calculated last day, and the end date Day is set to the day component of the calculated last day

rules.rule_name: Embed Calculated Start and End Dates into Monthly Report Job Parameters
rules.rule_description: Once the start date and end date for the Monthly report have been calculated, both dates must be embedded into the report job parameters before proceeding to job submission.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Embed Start Date and End Date
into Report Job Parameters

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Monthly report start date (first day of current month) and end date (last day of current month) have been successfully calculated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the report job for submission
acceptance_criteria.Then: The calculated start date is stored in both report job start date parameter slots (PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2), and the calculated end date is stored in both report job end date parameter slots (PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2), after which the system proceeds to the job submission confirmation step

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Current System Date for Yearly Report
rules.rule_description: When the Yearly report type is selected, the system must retrieve the current system date in order to determine the current calendar year, which will be used to compute both the start and end dates of the yearly report range.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Current System Date
to obtain Current Year

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type on the Transaction Report screen (the Yearly field is not empty and not low-values)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the ENTER key action for the Yearly report type
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and stores it in the working date field (WS-CURDATE-DATA), making the current year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) available for subsequent date range calculations

rules.rule_name: Set Yearly Report Start Date to January 1st of Current Year
rules.rule_description: For a Yearly report, the start date of the reporting period must always be the first day of the current calendar year — January 1st. The year component is derived from the current system date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Start Date
January 1st of Current Year
MM=01, DD=01, YYYY=Current Year

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type and the current system date has been retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the start date for the Yearly report
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Start Date is set with Month = '01' (January), Day = '01' (1st), and Year = the current calendar year obtained from the system date (WS-CURDATE-YEAR), forming a complete Start Date of YYYY-01-01

rules.rule_name: Set Yearly Report End Date to December 31st of Current Year
rules.rule_description: For a Yearly report, the end date of the reporting period must always be the last day of the current calendar year — December 31st. The year component is the same current year used for the start date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set End Date
December 31st of Current Year
MM=12, DD=31, YYYY=Current Year

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type and the current system date has been retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calculates the end date for the Yearly report
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End Date is set with Month = '12' (December), Day = '31' (31st), and Year = the current calendar year obtained from the system date (WS-CURDATE-YEAR), forming a complete End Date of YYYY-12-31

rules.rule_name: Store Calculated Yearly Start Date into Report Job Parameters
rules.rule_description: Once the Yearly report start date (January 1st of the current year) has been calculated, it must be stored into the report job submission parameters so that the print job uses the correct reporting period start boundary.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Store Calculated Start Date
into Report Job Parameters

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Yearly report start date has been calculated as January 1st of the current year (WS-START-DATE = YYYY-01-01)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the report job parameters for submission
acceptance_criteria.Then: The calculated start date (WS-START-DATE) is stored into both report job start date parameter slots: PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2, ensuring the print job receives the correct start date for the yearly reporting period

rules.rule_name: Store Calculated Yearly End Date into Report Job Parameters
rules.rule_description: Once the Yearly report end date (December 31st of the current year) has been calculated, it must be stored into the report job submission parameters so that the print job uses the correct reporting period end boundary.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Store Calculated End Date
into Report Job Parameters

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Yearly report end date has been calculated as December 31st of the current year (WS-END-DATE = YYYY-12-31)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the report job parameters for submission
acceptance_criteria.Then: The calculated end date (WS-END-DATE) is stored into both report job end date parameter slots: PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2, ensuring the print job receives the correct end date for the yearly reporting period

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Report Job Submission After Yearly Date Calculation
rules.rule_description: After all Yearly report date parameters have been calculated and stored, the system must set the report name to 'Yearly' and proceed to the report job submission process to queue the print job.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Yearly report type has been selected, the start date (January 1st of current year) and end date (December 31st of current year) have been calculated and stored into the report job parameters
acceptance_criteria.When: All date calculations and parameter assignments for the Yearly report are complete
acceptance_criteria.Then: The report name is set to 'Yearly' and the system proceeds to the report job submission process (SUBMIT-JOB-TO-INTRDR) to initiate the print job submission workflow

acceptance_criteria.When: The Start Date Month field (SDTMM) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'Start Date - Month can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Start Date Month field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

rules.rule_name: Custom Report - Start Day Field Must Not Be Empty
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Custom report type and the Start Month field has been validated as populated, the Start Date Day field must also contain a value. If it is left blank, an error message is displayed and the Start Day field is highlighted for correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Start Day Field Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, pressed ENTER, and the Start Date Month field has passed the empty-field validation check
acceptance_criteria.When: The Start Date Day field (SDTDD) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'Start Date - Day can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Start Date Day field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

rules.rule_name: Custom Report - Start Year Field Must Not Be Empty
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Custom report type and both the Start Month and Start Day fields have been validated as populated, the Start Date Year field must also contain a value. If it is left blank, an error message is displayed and the Start Year field is highlighted for correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Start Year Field Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, pressed ENTER, and both the Start Date Month and Start Date Day fields have passed the empty-field validation checks
acceptance_criteria.When: The Start Date Year field (SDTYYYY) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'Start Date - Year can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Start Date Year field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

rules.rule_name: Custom Report - End Month Field Must Not Be Empty
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Custom report type and all three Start Date fields have been validated as populated, the End Date Month field must also contain a value. If it is left blank, an error message is displayed and the End Month field is highlighted for correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is End Month Field Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, pressed ENTER, and all three Start Date fields (Month, Day, Year) have passed the empty-field validation checks
acceptance_criteria.When: The End Date Month field (EDTMM) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'End Date - Month can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the End Date Month field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

rules.rule_name: Custom Report - End Day Field Must Not Be Empty
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Custom report type and the Start Date fields plus the End Month field have been validated as populated, the End Date Day field must also contain a value. rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is End Day Field Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, pressed ENTER, and all three Start Date fields and the End Date Month field have passed the empty-field validation checks
acceptance_criteria.When: The End Date Day field (EDTDD) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'End Date - Day can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the End Date Day field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

rules.rule_name: Custom Report - End Year Field Must Not Be Empty
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Custom report type and all five preceding date fields have been validated as populated, the End Date Year field must also contain a value. If it is left blank, an error message is displayed and the End Year field is highlighted for correction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is End Year Field Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, pressed ENTER, and all five preceding date fields (Start Month, Start Day, Start Year, End Month, End Day) have passed the empty-field validation checks
acceptance_criteria.When: The End Date Year field (EDTYYYY) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'End Date - Year can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the End Date Year field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

rules.rule_name: Custom Report - All Six Date Fields Populated - Proceed to Numeric Validation
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Custom report type and all six date fields (Start Month, Start Day, Start Year, End Month, End Day, End Year) have been confirmed as non-empty, the system proceeds to the next stage of validation which checks that each field contains a valid numeric value within an acceptable range.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All Six Date Fields Are Populated Proceed to Numeric Validation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and pressed ENTER to submit the Transaction Report screen
acceptance_criteria.When: All six date fields — Start Date Month (SDTMM), Start Date Day (SDTDD), Start Date Year (SDTYYYY), End Date Month (EDTMM), End Date Day (EDTDD), and End Date Year (EDTYYYY) — are all populated with non-blank values

rules.rule_name: Convert Start Month Input to Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: Before validating the custom report Start Month, the system converts the user-entered Start Month text input into a pure numeric value so it can be evaluated against valid month range criteria.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Convert Start Month Input to Numeric Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and the Start Month field contains a user-entered text value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins numeric conversion of the custom date fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Start Month input value is converted to its numeric equivalent using a numeric evaluation function and the converted numeric value is stored back into the Start Month field, replacing the original text input

rules.rule_name: Validate Start Month is Numeric and Within Valid Range
rules.rule_description: After numeric conversion, the system validates that the Start Month value is a proper numeric value and falls within the valid calendar month range of 1 through 12. If either condition fails, an error is raised and the screen is redisplayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Start Month Is Numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a custom date range and the Start Month field has been converted to a numeric value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Start Month value is numeric AND is less than or equal to 12
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Start Month value is NOT numeric OR is greater than 12, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Start Date - Not a valid Month...', highlights the Start Month input field by positioning the cursor on it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; if the Start Month is valid, processing continues to Start Day conversion

rules.rule_name: Convert Start Day Input to Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: After the Start Month passes numeric validation, the system converts the user-entered Start Day text input into a pure numeric value so it can be evaluated against valid day range criteria.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Convert Start Day Input to Numeric Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and the Start Month has passed numeric validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to convert the Start Day field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Start Day input value is converted to its numeric equivalent using a numeric evaluation function and the converted numeric value is stored back into the Start Day field, replacing the original text input

rules.rule_name: Validate Start Day is Numeric and Within Valid Range
rules.rule_description: After numeric conversion, the system validates that the Start Day value is a proper numeric value and falls within the valid calendar day range of 1 through 31. If either condition fails, an error is raised and the screen is redisplayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Start Day Is Numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a custom date range and the Start Day field has been converted to a numeric value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Start Day value is numeric AND is less than or equal to 31
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Start Day value is NOT numeric OR is greater than 31, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Start Date - Not a valid Day...', highlights the Start Day input field by positioning the cursor on it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; if the Start Day is valid, processing continues to Start Year conversion

rules.rule_name: Convert Start Year Input to Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: After the Start Day passes numeric validation, the system converts the user-entered Start Year text input into a pure numeric value so it can be evaluated for numeric validity. The Start Year field accepts up to four digits.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Convert Start Year Input to Numeric Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and both Start Month and Start Day have passed numeric validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to convert the Start Year field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Start Year input value is converted to its numeric equivalent using a numeric evaluation function and the converted numeric value (up to 4 digits) is stored back into the Start Year field, replacing the original text input

rules.rule_name: Validate Start Year is Numeric
rules.rule_description: After numeric conversion, the system validates that the Start Year value is a proper numeric value. No upper or lower range limit is applied to the year; only numeric integrity is checked.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Start Year Is Numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a custom date range and the Start Year field has been converted to a numeric value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Start Year value is numeric
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Start Year value is NOT numeric, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Start Date - Not a valid Year...', highlights the Start Year input field by positioning the cursor on it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; if the Start Year is valid, processing continues to End Month conversion

rules.rule_name: Convert End Month Input to Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: After all Start Date fields pass numeric validation, the system converts the user-entered End Month text input into a pure numeric value so it can be evaluated against valid month range criteria.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Convert End Month Input to Numeric Value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and all three Start Date fields (Month, Day, Year) have passed numeric validation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to convert the End Month field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End Month input value is converted to its numeric equivalent using a numeric evaluation function and the converted numeric value is stored back into the End Month field, replacing the original text input

rules.rule_name: Validate End Month is Numeric and Within Valid Range
rules.rule_description: After numeric conversion, the system validates that the End Month value is a proper numeric value and falls within the valid calendar month range of 1 through 12. If either condition fails, an error is raised and the screen is redisplayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End Month Is Numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a custom date range and the End Month field has been converted to a numeric value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the End Month value is numeric AND is less than or equal to 12
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the End Month value is NOT numeric OR is greater than 12, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'End Date - Not a valid Month...', highlights the End Month input field by positioning the cursor on it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; if the End Month is valid, processing continues to End Day conversion

rules.rule_name: Convert End Day Input to Numeric Value

rules.rule_name: Invoke Date Validation Utility for Custom Start Date
rules.rule_description: When a user selects the Custom report type and provides a start date, the system must invoke the CSUTLDTC date validation utility by preparing the start date in YYYY-MM-DD format along with the expected date format, then calling the utility to determine whether the date is a real calendar date.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The CSUTLDTC utility is called with the assembled start date and date format, and the validation result (including severity code and message number) is returned for further evaluation

rules.rule_name: Accept Custom Start Date When Validation Utility Returns Success
rules.rule_description: After the CSUTLDTC date validation utility is called for the custom start date, if the utility returns a severity code of '0000', the start date is confirmed as a valid calendar date and processing continues to the end date validation step.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The start date is accepted as valid and processing continues to the end date calendar validity check without any error message or screen redisplay

rules.rule_name: Treat Known Validation Exception as Valid for Custom Start Date
rules.rule_description: When the CSUTLDTC utility returns a non-success severity code for the custom start date, the system checks whether the returned message number is '2513', which represents a known and acceptable exception. If so, the date is treated as valid and processing continues.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The start date is treated as valid despite the non-success severity code, no error message is displayed, and processing continues to the end date calendar validity check

rules.rule_name: Reject Custom Start Date When It Is Not a Real Calendar Date

rules.rule_name: Custom End Date - Prepare Date for Calendar Validation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and has entered values for End Date Year (EDTYYYYI), End Date Month (EDTMMI), and End Date Day (EDTDDI) on the Transaction Report screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the end date for calendar validation after all numeric range checks have passed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system assembles the end date by moving the user-entered End Date Year into WS-END-DATE-YYYY, End Date Month into WS-END-DATE-MM, and End Date Day into WS-END-DATE-DD, forming a complete date value (WS-END-DATE) in YYYY-MM-DD format, which is then loaded into the date validation input field (CSUTLDTC-DATE) along with the expected date format (CSUTLDTC-DATE-FORMAT)

rules.rule_name: Custom End Date - Invoke Calendar Date Validation Utility
rules.rule_description: The system invokes the external date validation utility CSUTLDTC to determine whether the user-entered custom end date represents a real, existing calendar date. This utility receives the assembled end date and its expected format, and returns a validation result including a severity code and message number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Call CSUTLDTC Date Validation Utility with End Date and Date Format

acceptance_criteria.Given: The custom end date has been assembled in YYYY-MM-DD format and loaded into CSUTLDTC-DATE, and the date format has been loaded into CSUTLDTC-DATE-FORMAT, and the result area (CSUTLDTC-RESULT) has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calls the CSUTLDTC date validation utility passing the end date (CSUTLDTC-DATE), the date format (CSUTLDTC-DATE-FORMAT), and the result area (CSUTLDTC-RESULT)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The CSUTLDTC utility processes the end date and populates CSUTLDTC-RESULT with a severity code (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD) and a message number (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM) indicating whether the end date is a valid calendar date

rules.rule_name: Custom End Date - Evaluate Calendar Validity Result
rules.rule_description: After the date validation utility returns its result, the system evaluates the severity code to determine whether the custom end date is a real calendar date. A severity code of '0000' indicates the date is valid. Any other severity code, except for message number '2513', indicates the date is not a valid calendar date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is End Date Calendar Valid? Severity Code = 0000?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The CSUTLDTC date validation utility has been called and has returned a result containing a severity code (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD) and a message number (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM) for the custom end date
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the severity code returned by the CSUTLDTC utility
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the severity code equals '0000', the end date is considered a valid calendar date and processing continues to the next step; if the severity code is anything other than '0000' AND the message number is NOT '2513', the end date is considered invalid and the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Not a valid date...', highlights the End Date Month field (EDTMML) with cursor positioning (-1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen with the error; if the severity code is not '0000' but the message number IS '2513', no error is raised and processing continues

rules.rule_name: Custom End Date - Display Calendar Validation Error
rules.rule_description: When the custom end date fails calendar validation (i.e., the date does not exist in the real calendar, such as February 30), the system informs the user with a specific error message and highlights the End Date Month field to guide the user to correct the invalid date entry.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The CSUTLDTC date validation utility has returned a severity code other than '0000' AND a message number other than '2513' for the custom end date entered by the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines that the custom end date is not a real calendar date
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error message (WS-MESSAGE) to 'End Date - Not a valid date...', sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y' to indicate an error condition, positions the cursor on the End Date Month field (EDTMML set to -1) to highlight the error location, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen showing the error message so the user can correct the end date entry
