rules.rule_name: Monthly Report End Date Calculation
rules.rule_description: When a Monthly report type is selected, the system automatically calculates the end date as the last day of the current calendar month by advancing to the first day of the next month and subtracting one day.

Validated Start Date
YYYY-MM-DD

acceptance_criteria.When: The system assembles the custom report start date

rules.rule_name: Custom Report End Date Assignment from User Input
rules.rule_description: When a Custom report type is selected, the system uses the user-entered and validated end date fields (year, month, day) to construct the end date for the report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Take User-Entered
Validated End Date
YYYY-MM-DD

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and has entered valid values for the end date fields: End Year (EDTYYYYI), End Month (EDTMMI), and End Day (EDTDDI), all of which have passed all empty-field, numeric, range, and calendar validity checks
acceptance_criteria.When: The system assembles the custom report end date
acceptance_criteria.Then: The end date is constructed by combining the user-entered End Year into WS-END-DATE-YYYY, End Month into WS-END-DATE-MM, and End Day into WS-END-DATE-DD, resulting in a complete end date in YYYY-MM-DD format

rules.rule_name: Embed Start Date into JCL Parameter Fields
rules.rule_description: Regardless of the report type selected (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), the calculated or validated start date must be embedded into both JCL start date parameter fields (PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2) to ensure the batch job uses the correct reporting period start date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Embed Start Date into
JCL Parameter Fields
PARM-START-DATE-1
PARM-START-DATE-2

acceptance_criteria.Given: A report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom) has been selected and the corresponding start date has been determined — either calculated by the system (Monthly/Yearly) or entered and validated by the user (Custom)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the JCL records for batch job submission
acceptance_criteria.Then: The start date value (WS-START-DATE in YYYY-MM-DD format) is copied into both JCL parameter fields PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2, so that the batch job receives the correct start date of the reporting period in both parameter positions

rules.rule_name: Embed End Date into JCL Parameter Fields
rules.rule_description: Regardless of the report type selected (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), the calculated or validated end date must be embedded into both JCL end date parameter fields (PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2) to ensure the batch job uses the correct reporting period end date.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Embed End Date into

PARM-END-DATE-2

acceptance_criteria.Given: A report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom) has been selected and the corresponding end date has been determined — either calculated by the system (Monthly/Yearly) or entered and validated by the user (Custom)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the JCL records for batch job submission
acceptance_criteria.Then: The end date value (WS-END-DATE in YYYY-MM-DD format) is copied into both JCL parameter fields PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2, so that the batch job receives the correct end date of the reporting period in both parameter positions

rules.rule_name: JCL Records Ready for Job Submission After Date Embedding
rules.rule_description: Once both the start and end dates have been embedded into all four JCL parameter fields, the JCL records are considered complete and ready to be submitted to the internal job reader queue for batch processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
JCL Records Now Contain
Correct Date Parameters
Ready for Job Submission

acceptance_criteria.Given: The start date has been embedded into PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2, and the end date has been embedded into PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2 for the selected report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom)
acceptance_criteria.When: All date parameters have been successfully populated in the JCL records
acceptance_criteria.Then: The JCL records are considered fully prepared with the correct date parameters and the process proceeds to the job submission step, where the JCL records will be written to the JOBS transient data queue (internal reader) for batch execution

rules.rule_name: Report Type Determines Date Source for JCL Construction
rules.rule_description: The source of the start and end dates used in JCL construction is determined by the report type selected by the user: Monthly and Yearly report types use system-calculated dates, while the Custom report type uses user-entered and validated dates.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Which Report
Type?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Transaction Report screen with a report type selected
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the selected report type to determine the date source for JCL parameter construction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system applies the following decision: (1) If Monthly is selected — use system-calculated dates (first and last day of current month); (2) If Yearly is selected — use system-calculated dates (January 1st and December 31st of current year); (3) If Custom is selected — use the user-entered and fully validated start and end dates; in all cases, the determined dates are then embedded into the JCL parameter fields PARM-START-DATE-1, PARM-START-DATE-2, PARM-END-DATE-1, and PARM-END-DATE-2

rules.rule_name: Initialize Batch Job Submission Processing
rules.rule_description: When a report job is confirmed for submission, the system initializes the JCL record processing by starting from the very first record in the job definition list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Begin Processing JCL Records
Start from First Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has confirmed the report submission with 'Y' or 'y' in the confirmation field and no prior errors exist
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the batch job submission process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system initializes the JCL record processing starting from the first record (index position 1) in the job definition list, with the end-of-loop indicator set to 'No' so that processing can begin

rules.rule_name: Enforce Maximum JCL Record Processing Limit
rules.rule_description: The system enforces a maximum limit of 1000 JCL records that can be processed during a single batch job submission to prevent runaway processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
More Records to Process?
Up to 1000 Records

acceptance_criteria.Given: The batch job submission process is actively writing JCL records to the JOBS queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether more records remain to be processed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system continues processing only if the current record index is 1000 or fewer AND the end-of-loop indicator is 'No' AND no errors have occurred; if the record index exceeds 1000, processing stops and the job submission is considered complete

rules.rule_name: Read Next JCL Record from Job Definition
rules.rule_description: During batch job submission, the system sequentially reads each JCL record from the job definition list using the current index position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next JCL Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The batch job submission loop is active, the record count is within the 1000-record limit, no end-of-file condition has been set, and no errors have occurred
acceptance_criteria.When: The system retrieves the next JCL record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads the JCL record at the current index position from the job lines collection (JOB-LINES) and loads it into the active JCL record buffer (JCL-RECORD) for further processing

rules.rule_name: Detect End-of-Job Marker or Blank Record
rules.rule_description: After reading each JCL record, the system checks whether the record signals the end of the job definition, either through an explicit end-of-file marker or by being blank/empty.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Record an
EOF Marker or
Blank/Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A JCL record has been read from the job definition list into the active record buffer
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the content of the current JCL record
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the record contains the end-of-file marker '/*EOF', or the record contains only spaces, or the record contains only low-values (empty binary content), the system sets the end-of-loop indicator to 'Yes' to stop further processing; otherwise, the record is treated as a valid JCL record and submitted to the queue

rules.rule_name: Stop JCL Record Processing on End-of-File or Limit Reached
rules.rule_description: The system terminates JCL record processing when either an end-of-file condition is detected or the maximum record limit of 1000 has been reached, signaling that the job submission sequence is complete.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Stop Processing
No More Records to Submit

acceptance_criteria.Given: The batch job submission loop is active
acceptance_criteria.When: Either the current JCL record is an EOF marker ('/*EOF') or blank/empty, OR the record index has exceeded 1000 records
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system exits the JCL record processing loop and proceeds to finalize the job submission, with no further records written to the JOBS queue

rules.rule_name: Write JCL Record to JOBS Internal Reader Queue
rules.rule_description: Each valid JCL record is written to the JOBS transient data queue, which acts as the internal reader to trigger batch job execution for the transaction report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Write JCL Record to
JOBS Internal Reader Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid JCL record has been read (not an EOF marker and not blank/empty) and the record index is within the 1000-record limit
acceptance_criteria.When: The system submits the current JCL record to the batch job queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system writes the JCL record from the active record buffer (JCL-RECORD) to the JOBS transient data queue with the full record length, making it available to the internal reader for batch job execution

rules.rule_name: Handle Failure to Write JCL Record to JOBS Queue
rules.rule_description: If the system fails to write a JCL record to the JOBS internal reader queue, an error is raised, the submission is halted, and the user is notified that the job could not be submitted.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Write to
JOBS Queue
Successful?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write a JCL record to the JOBS transient data queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The write operation does not complete successfully (response code is not NORMAL)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Unable to Write TDQ (JOBS)...' on the report screen, positions the cursor on the Monthly field, and stops further JCL record processing; the batch job is not submitted

rules.rule_name: Confirm Successful Write and Advance to Next JCL Record
rules.rule_description: When a JCL record is successfully written to the JOBS queue, the system advances the record index to process the next record in sequence.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Move to
Next JCL Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A JCL record has been successfully written to the JOBS transient data queue with a NORMAL response
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the write was successful
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system increments the record index by 1 and returns to check whether more records remain to be processed, continuing the sequential submission of JCL records

rules.rule_name: Complete Batch Job Submission
rules.rule_description: Once all JCL records have been written to the JOBS queue without errors, the batch job submission is considered complete and control returns to the report screen with a success confirmation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End: Job Submission Complete

acceptance_criteria.Given: All JCL records up to the EOF marker or the 1000-record limit have been processed and written to the JOBS queue with no errors
acceptance_criteria.When: The batch job submission loop exits normally
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system considers the job submission complete; control returns to the calling process (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY), which then clears all input fields, displays a success message in green reading '[Report Name] report submitted for printing ...' on the transaction report screen, and repositions the cursor on the Monthly field

acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether any errors were flagged during the entire submission process

rules.rule_name: Clear All Input Fields After Successful Job Submission
rules.rule_description: Upon successful job submission with no errors, all user input fields on the Transaction Report screen are reset to their initial empty state, including report type selectors, all custom date fields, and the confirmation field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

rules.rule_name: Set Success Message Display Color to Green
rules.rule_description: The success confirmation message is visually distinguished from error messages by displaying it in green color on the Transaction Report screen, providing a clear positive visual indicator to the user.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The job submission has completed successfully with no errors detected and all input fields have been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the success notification message for display

rules.rule_name: Assign Report Name 'Yearly' for Yearly Report Type

rules.rule_name: Assign Report Name 'Custom' for Custom Date Range Report Type
rules.rule_description: When the user selects the Custom date range report option, the internal report name is set to 'Custom', which is subsequently used to build the success confirmation message displayed to the user.

rules.rule_name: Build Dynamic Success Message Based on Submitted Report Type
rules.rule_description: The success confirmation message is dynamically constructed by combining the report type name with a standard confirmation phrase, resulting in a report-type-specific message such as 'Monthly report submitted for printing...', 'Yearly report submitted for printing...', or 'Custom report submitted for printing...'

rules.rule_name: Display Transaction Report Screen with Green Success Message and Cursor on Monthly Field
rules.rule_description: After building the success message, the Transaction Report screen is refreshed and displayed to the user showing the green success confirmation message, with the cursor automatically positioned on the Monthly report selector field, ready for the user's next action.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has triggered an All Fields Initialization event, either following a successful report job submission or when the user cancels a report submission by entering 'N' in the confirmation field
acceptance_criteria.When: The initialization routine executes the reset of Start Date input fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Start Date Month field (SDTMMI) is reset to its default empty state, the Start Date Day field (SDTDDI) is reset to its default empty state, and the Start Date Year field (SDTYYYYI) is reset to its default empty state — ensuring no previously entered start date values persist on the screen

rules.rule_name: Reset End Date Fields During Field Initialization
rules.rule_description: When the screen fields are initialized, all three components of the custom report End Date — Month, Day, and Year — must be cleared to their empty/default state so no previously entered end date values remain visible on the refreshed screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear End Date Fields
Reset End Month
Reset End Day
Reset End Year

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has triggered an All Fields Initialization event, either following a successful report job submission or when the user cancels a report submission by entering 'N' in the confirmation field
acceptance_criteria.When: The initialization routine executes the reset of End Date input fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End Date Month field (EDTMMI) is reset to its default empty state, the End Date Day field (EDTDDI) is reset to its default empty state, and the End Date Year field (EDTYYYYI) is reset to its default empty state — ensuring no previously entered end date values persist on the screen

rules.rule_name: Reset Confirmation and Message Fields During Field Initialization
rules.rule_description: When the screen fields are initialized, the print confirmation field and the screen message area must both be cleared to their empty/default state, ensuring no prior confirmation input or status message remains displayed on the refreshed screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Remaining Fields
Reset Confirmation Field
Reset Message Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has triggered an All Fields Initialization event, either following a successful report job submission or when the user cancels a report submission by entering 'N' in the confirmation field
acceptance_criteria.When: The initialization routine executes the reset of the confirmation and message fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The print confirmation input field (CONFIRMI) is reset to its default empty state, and the screen message area (WS-MESSAGE) is reset to its default empty state — ensuring no prior confirmation value or informational/error message remains visible to the user

rules.rule_name: Set Cursor Focus to Monthly Report Field After Initialization
rules.rule_description: After all screen fields have been initialized/reset, the screen cursor must be automatically positioned on the Monthly report selector field. This guides the user to begin their next report selection from the first available report type option.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Cursor Focus
to Monthly Report Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed resetting all screen input fields — report type selectors, start date fields, end date fields, confirmation field, and message area — as part of the All Fields Initialization routine
acceptance_criteria.When: The initialization routine sets the cursor position for the refreshed screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor focus is set to the Monthly report selector field (MONTHLYL is set to -1), so that when the Transaction Report screen is next displayed, the cursor is automatically positioned on the Monthly field, ready for the user's next report type selection

rules.rule_name: Default Target Screen When No Destination Is Specified
rules.rule_description: When navigation to a previous screen is triggered but no target screen has been set in the communication area, the system defaults the destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default Target Screen to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The navigation to a previous screen has been initiated and the target program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) in the communication area contains LOW-VALUES or SPACES, indicating no destination has been specified
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the target program field before transferring control
acceptance_criteria.Then: The target program is set to the Sign-On screen identifier 'COSGN00C' so that navigation proceeds to a valid default destination

rules.rule_name: Record Originating Transaction ID Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to another screen, the system records the current transaction identifier into the communication area so the destination screen knows which transaction initiated the navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Transaction ID as Originating Transaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to navigate away from the Transaction Report screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The navigation procedure is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is recorded as the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the shared communication area passed to the destination screen

rules.rule_name: Record Originating Program Name Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to another screen, the system records the current program name into the communication area so the destination screen knows which program initiated the navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program Name as Originating Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to navigate away from the Transaction Report screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The navigation procedure is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is recorded as the originating program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) in the shared communication area passed to the destination screen

rules.rule_name: Reset Program Context on Navigation
rules.rule_description: When navigating away from the Transaction Report screen, the program context indicator in the communication area is reset to zero, ensuring the destination screen starts with a clean context state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has recorded the originating transaction ID and program name in the communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The navigation procedure prepares to transfer control to the target screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program context field (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) in the communication area is set to ZEROS before control is transferred

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Sign-On Screen When No Active Session Exists
rules.rule_description: When a user accesses the Transaction Report screen without an active session (no communication area data from a prior screen), the system redirects the user to the Sign-On screen to establish a valid session before proceeding.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction Report screen is accessed and the communication area length (EIBCALEN) equals zero, indicating no active session exists
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the session state at program entry
acceptance_criteria.Then: The target screen is set to the Sign-On screen 'COSGN00C' and control is transferred to that screen, passing the communication area containing the originating transaction ID and program name

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Main Menu When User Presses PF3
rules.rule_description: When the user explicitly requests to go back by pressing the PF3 key on the Transaction Report screen, the system transfers control to the Main Menu screen, passing along the session context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Main Menu Screen COMEN01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen with an active session and has received the screen input
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The target screen is set to the Main Menu screen 'COMEN01C' and control is transferred to that screen, passing the communication area containing the originating transaction ID and program name

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Target Screen with Communication Area
rules.rule_description: The actual transfer of control to the destination screen is performed by invoking the target program and passing the full communication area, which carries session context including the originating transaction ID and program name.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The target screen has been determined (either Sign-On screen 'COSGN00C' or Main Menu screen 'COMEN01C'), and the originating transaction ID and program name have been recorded in the communication area, and the program context has been reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the screen transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the identified target program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) and the full communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) — containing the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), originating program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), and reset program context (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = ZEROS) — is passed to the destination screen

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No active session communication area exists (EIBCALEN = 0), indicating this is the very first call with no prior session context
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and transfers control to the previous screen navigation routine, preventing unauthorized access to the report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session Validation on Program Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user accesses the Transaction Report screen without an active session (no communication area), they must be redirected to the Sign-On screen to authenticate first.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user navigates to the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An active session communication area exists (EIBCALEN is greater than 0)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system loads the full contents of the communication area (DFHCOMMAREA) into the working session data area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) to restore the user's session context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Existing Session Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user accesses the Transaction Report screen with an active session, the system restores the existing session context from the communication area to maintain continuity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has an active session and navigates to the Transaction Report screen for the first time (program re-entry flag is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects this is not a re-entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is false)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the re-entry flag to TRUE, initializes the output screen map (CORPT0AO) to LOW-VALUES (blank), positions the cursor on the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), and sends the Transaction Report screen with an erase command to display a clean screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initial Transaction Report Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the first visit to the Transaction Report screen within a session, the screen is presented in a clean state with all fields blank and the cursor positioned on the Monthly report option to guide the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has previously been presented the Transaction Report screen and has entered data or pressed a key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects this is a re-entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system receives the screen input from map CORPT0A in mapset CORPT00 into the input data area (CORPT0AI), capturing all user-entered field values for subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive User Input from Transaction Report Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: On subsequent visits (re-entries), the system retrieves all user-entered data from the Transaction Report screen before processing any actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen and has received the screen input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER (DFHENTER) or PF3 (DFHPF3)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', positions the cursor on the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), sets the error message to the invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) stored in WS-MESSAGE, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Key Press Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3, the system rejects the action and informs the user that the key pressed is not valid for this screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key (DFHPF3)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Main Menu (COMEN01C) and performs the return-to-previous-screen routine, transferring control to the Main Menu with the current communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate Back to Main Menu via PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: Pressing PF3 on the Transaction Report screen returns the user to the Main Menu screen, allowing them to exit without submitting a report.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen and presses the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: None of the report type fields are selected — Monthly (MONTHLYI), Yearly (YEARLYI), and Custom (CUSTOMI) are all spaces or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Select a report type to print report...', positions the cursor on the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Report Type Selection Requirement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The user must select one of the available report types (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom) before the system can proceed with report submission. Pressing ENTER without a selection is not permitted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Monthly report type (MONTHLYI is not spaces or LOW-VALUES) and pressed ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Monthly report selection
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current date, sets the report name to 'Monthly', assigns the current year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) to WS-START-DATE-YYYY, assigns the current month (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) to WS-START-DATE-MM, assigns '01' to WS-START-DATE-DD, and copies WS-START-DATE to both PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2

all_rules.Rule_Name: Monthly Report Start Date Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Monthly report type is selected, the system automatically determines the start date as the first day of the current calendar month, eliminating the need for manual date entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Monthly report start date has been set to the first day of the current month
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the end date for the Monthly report
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the day to 1, adds 1 to the current month; if the resulting month exceeds 12, it increments the year by 1 and resets the month to 1; then computes the end date as one day before the first day of the next month using DATE-OF-INTEGER and INTEGER-OF-DATE functions; assigns the resulting year, month, and day to WS-END-DATE-YYYY, WS-END-DATE-MM, and WS-END-DATE-DD respectively; and copies WS-END-DATE to both PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2

all_rules.Rule_Name: Monthly Report End Date Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Monthly report type is selected, the system automatically calculates the last day of the current calendar month as the end date, correctly handling month-end boundaries and year rollovers.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type (YEARLYI is not spaces or LOW-VALUES) and pressed ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Yearly report selection
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current date, sets the report name to 'Yearly', assigns the current year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) to WS-START-DATE-YYYY, assigns '01' to WS-START-DATE-MM, assigns '01' to WS-START-DATE-DD, and copies WS-START-DATE to both PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2

all_rules.Rule_Name: Yearly Report Start Date Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Yearly report type is selected, the system automatically sets the start date to January 1st of the current year.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Yearly report start date has been set to January 1st of the current year
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the end date for the Yearly report
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system assigns the current year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) to WS-END-DATE-YYYY, assigns '12' to WS-END-DATE-MM, assigns '31' to WS-END-DATE-DD, and copies WS-END-DATE to both PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2

all_rules.Rule_Name: Yearly Report End Date Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Yearly report type is selected, the system automatically sets the end date to December 31st of the current year.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type (CUSTOMI is not spaces or LOW-VALUES) and pressed ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Start Date Month field (SDTMMI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Month can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the Start Month field (SDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - Start Month Empty Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Custom report type is selected, the Start Date Month field is mandatory and must not be left blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and the Start Date Month field has been provided
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Start Date Day field (SDTDDI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Day can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the Start Day field (SDTDDL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - Start Day Empty Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Custom report type is selected, the Start Date Day field is mandatory and must not be left blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and both Start Date Month and Day fields have been provided
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Start Date Year field (SDTYYYYI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Year can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the Start Year field (SDTYYYYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - Start Year Empty Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Custom report type is selected, the Start Date Year field is mandatory and must not be left blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all three Start Date fields have been provided
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End Date Month field (EDTMMI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Month can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the End Month field (EDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - End Month Empty Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Custom report type is selected, the End Date Month field is mandatory and must not be left blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and Start Date fields plus End Date Month have been provided
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End Date Day field (EDTDDI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Day can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the End Day field (EDTDDL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - End Day Empty Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Custom report type is selected, the End Date Day field is mandatory and must not be left blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all five other date fields have been provided
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End Date Year field (EDTYYYYI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Year can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the End Year field (EDTYYYYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - End Year Empty Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Custom report type is selected, the End Date Year field is mandatory and must not be left blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all six date fields (SDTMMI, SDTDDI, SDTYYYYI, EDTMMI, EDTDDI, EDTYYYYI) are non-empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to numeric validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system uses NUMVAL-C function to convert each of the six date fields to their numeric values: Start Month and End Month are stored as 2-digit numbers (WS-NUM-99), Start Day and End Day are stored as 2-digit numbers (WS-NUM-99), and Start Year and End Year are stored as 4-digit numbers (WS-NUM-9999); the converted values are moved back into their respective input fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - Numeric Conversion of Date Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: After confirming all six custom date fields are non-empty, the system converts each field to its numeric equivalent to prepare for range and validity checks.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all date fields have been converted to numeric values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Start Date Month (SDTMMI of CORPT0AI) is not numeric OR its value is greater than '12'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Not a valid Month...', positions the cursor on the Start Month field (SDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - Start Month Range Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Start Date Month entered for a Custom report must be a valid numeric month value between 1 and 12.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all date fields have been converted to numeric values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Start Date Day (SDTDDI of CORPT0AI) is not numeric OR its value is greater than '31'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Not a valid Day...', positions the cursor on the Start Day field (SDTDDL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - Start Day Range Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Start Date Day entered for a Custom report must be a valid numeric day value between 1 and 31.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all date fields have been converted to numeric values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Start Date Year (SDTYYYYI of CORPT0AI) is not numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Not a valid Year...', positions the cursor on the Start Year field (SDTYYYYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - Start Year Numeric Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Start Date Year entered for a Custom report must contain a valid numeric value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all date fields have been converted to numeric values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End Date Month (EDTMMI of CORPT0AI) is not numeric OR its value is greater than '12'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Not a valid Month...', positions the cursor on the End Month field (EDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - End Month Range Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The End Date Month entered for a Custom report must be a valid numeric month value between 1 and 12.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all date fields have been converted to numeric values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End Date Day (EDTDDI of CORPT0AI) is not numeric OR its value is greater than '31'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Not a valid Day...', positions the cursor on the End Day field (EDTDDL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - End Day Range Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The End Date Day entered for a Custom report must be a valid numeric day value between 1 and 31.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all date fields have been converted to numeric values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End Date Year (EDTYYYYI of CORPT0AI) is not numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Not a valid Year...', positions the cursor on the End Year field (EDTYYYYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Date Range - End Year Numeric Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The End Date Year entered for a Custom report must contain a valid numeric value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a Custom report date range and all numeric and range validations have passed for the Start Date fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assembles the Start Date from SDTYYYYI, SDTMMI, and SDTDDI into WS-START-DATE and calls the external date validation program CSUTLDTC with the date and date format (WS-DATE-FORMAT)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the validation result severity code (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD) is '0000', the Start Date is valid and processing continues; if the severity code is not '0000' AND the message number (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM) is not '2513', the system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Start Date - Not a valid date...', positions the cursor on the Start Month field (SDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Start Date Calendar Validity Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: After numeric and range validations pass, the custom Start Date must represent a real calendar date (e.g., February 30 is not a valid calendar date). An external date validation service is invoked to confirm this.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The custom Start Date has passed calendar validity and the End Date fields (EDTYYYYI, EDTMMI, EDTDDI) have passed numeric and range validations
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assembles the End Date from EDTYYYYI, EDTMMI, and EDTDDI into WS-END-DATE and calls the external date validation program CSUTLDTC with the date and date format (WS-DATE-FORMAT)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the validation result severity code (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD) is '0000', the End Date is valid and processing continues; if the severity code is not '0000' AND the message number (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM) is not '2513', the system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Not a valid date...', positions the cursor on the End Month field (EDTMML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom End Date Calendar Validity Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Start Date is validated as a real calendar date, the custom End Date must also represent a real calendar date. An external date validation service is invoked to confirm this.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom) has been selected and all date validations have passed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Confirmation field (CONFIRMI of CORPT0AI) is spaces or LOW-VALUES (left empty by the user)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', constructs the message 'Please confirm to print the [WS-REPORT-NAME] report...' using the selected report name, positions the cursor on the Confirmation field (CONFIRML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen awaiting user confirmation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Report Print Confirmation Prompt
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before submitting any report job for printing, the system requires the user to explicitly confirm the action by entering a value in the confirmation field. An empty confirmation field triggers a prompt.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A report type has been selected, all validations have passed, and the user has entered a value in the Confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Confirmation field (CONFIRMI of CORPT0AI) contains 'N' or 'n'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs the initialize-all-fields routine which resets all screen input fields (MONTHLYI, YEARLYI, CUSTOMI, SDTMMI, SDTDDI, SDTYYYYI, EDTMMI, EDTDDI, EDTYYYYI, CONFIRMI, WS-MESSAGE) to their initial empty state, sets the cursor to the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), sets the error flag to 'Y', and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Report Submission Cancellation via Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user enters 'N' or 'n' in the confirmation field, the report submission is cancelled, all input fields are cleared, and the screen is refreshed for a new selection.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A report type has been selected, all validations have passed, and the user has entered a value in the Confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Confirmation field (CONFIRMI of CORPT0AI) contains any value other than 'Y', 'y', 'N', or 'n'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', constructs the error message by concatenating '"', the entered confirmation value (CONFIRMI), and '" is not a valid value to confirm...' into WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the Confirmation field (CONFIRML = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Confirmation Value Rejection
all_rules.Rule_Description: The confirmation field only accepts 'Y', 'y', 'N', or 'n'. Any other value entered is rejected with an informative error message showing the invalid value entered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has confirmed the report submission with 'Y' or 'y' and no errors exist
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the batch job for submission
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies WS-START-DATE to both PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2, and copies WS-END-DATE to both PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2, embedding the date range parameters into the JCL job records (JOB-LINES) that will be submitted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Batch Job JCL Preparation with Date Parameters
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the user confirms the report submission, the system prepares the batch job by embedding the calculated or entered start and end dates into the job parameters before submission.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has confirmed the report submission and the JCL records have been prepared with the correct date parameters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system iterates through JOB-LINES records from index 1 up to a maximum of 1000 records, writing each JCL-RECORD to the JOBS transient data queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each record is written to the JOBS queue; the loop terminates when a record equals '/*EOF' or is spaces or LOW-VALUES; if all records are written successfully, processing continues to the success notification; if any write operation fails, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets the error message to 'Unable to Write TDQ (JOBS)...', positions the cursor on the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Batch Job Submission to Internal Reader
all_rules.Rule_Description: The prepared batch report job is submitted for execution by writing JCL records sequentially to the JOBS internal reader queue. The process continues until all records are written or an end-of-file marker is encountered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The report job has been successfully written to the JOBS queue and no error flag is set (ERR-FLG-ON is false)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the job submission process without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system performs the initialize-all-fields routine to reset all screen input fields, sets the error message color to green (DFHGREEN) for ERRMSGC of CORPT0AO, constructs the success message by concatenating WS-REPORT-NAME (delimited by space) with ' report submitted for printing ...' into WS-MESSAGE, positions the cursor on the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen with the green success message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Report Job Submission Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a report job is successfully submitted to the print queue with no errors, the user receives a clear visual confirmation in green text, and all input fields are reset for a potential new submission.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Report screen is about to be sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the populate-header-info routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current date and time, populates the screen header with: application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01 to TITLE01O), application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02 to TITLE02O), transaction name (WS-TRANID to TRNNAMEO), program name (WS-PGMNAME to PGMNAMEO), current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY to CURDATEO), and current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS to CURTIMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Population with Current Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the Transaction Report screen is displayed, the header section is refreshed with current system information including the application titles, transaction identifier, program name, and the current date and time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A report submission has been successfully completed or the user has cancelled the submission with 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the initialize-all-fields routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the cursor position to the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1) and initializes (clears to empty/default) all input fields: MONTHLYI, YEARLYI, CUSTOMI, SDTMMI, SDTDDI, SDTYYYYI, EDTMMI, EDTDDI, EDTYYYYI, CONFIRMI, and WS-MESSAGE

all_rules.Rule_Name: All Screen Input Fields Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a reset is required (after successful submission or cancellation), all screen input fields are cleared to their initial empty state and the cursor is repositioned to the Monthly report option field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system needs to navigate away from the Transaction Report screen (either due to no active session or PF3 key press)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return-to-previous-screen routine is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is LOW-VALUES or spaces, it defaults to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C); the system then sets CDEMO-FROM-TRANID to WS-TRANID, sets CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM to WS-PGMNAME, sets CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT to zeros, and transfers control to CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM via XCTL passing the CARDDEMO-COMMAREA

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigation to Previous Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating away from the Transaction Report screen, the system transfers control to the designated target program while preserving the session communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No active session communication area exists (session length equals zero), indicating the user has not yet signed on
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a first-time call with no valid session and initiates a redirect to the Sign-On screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect First-Time Program Call with No Active Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the user has an active session when entering the Transaction Report program. If no session communication area exists, the user has not yet authenticated and must be redirected.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that no active session exists (first-time program call)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The destination screen needs to be assigned for the redirect
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination program is set to the Sign-On screen identifier 'COSGN00C'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Default Destination to Sign-On Screen on First Call
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no active session exists, the system explicitly sets the navigation destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) so the user can authenticate before accessing the report functionality.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to redirect the user away from the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The destination program identifier is checked for validity
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the destination program identifier is empty or contains only low-values (uninitialized), the destination is considered not set and a default must be applied; if the destination is already set to a valid value, the system proceeds with that destination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate That a Destination Screen Has Been Assigned
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before redirecting the user, the system verifies that a valid destination screen has been assigned. This prevents navigation failures caused by an unset or blank destination program identifier.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to redirect the user and the destination program identifier is either empty or contains only low-values (uninitialized)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The destination validation check finds no valid destination has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The destination program is defaulted to the Sign-On screen identifier 'COSGN00C'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Default Sign-On Screen When Destination Is Not Set
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the destination screen identifier has not been assigned or is blank, the system defaults the navigation target to the Sign-On screen to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to redirect the user to another screen (Sign-On or other destination)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Navigation context is being prepared prior to the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction identifier is saved as the originating transaction, the current program name is saved as the originating program, and the program context counter is reset to zero

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Transaction and Program Name for Return Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring the user to another screen, the system records the current transaction identifier, program name, and resets the program context. This navigation breadcrumb allows the destination screen to know where the user came from and enables correct return navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination screen has been validated and set, and the navigation context (originating transaction and program) has been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program (Sign-On screen 'COSGN00C' or other valid destination) with the current session communication area passed along, and the Transaction Report program terminates its current execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redirect User to Destination Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system transfers control to the designated destination screen, passing the current session data. This ends the current program's execution and hands control entirely to the destination program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user accesses the Transaction Report screen and an active session communication area exists (session length is greater than zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms a valid session is present
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full session communication area data is loaded into the working session data area for use throughout the current program execution, using the exact length of the passed communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Existing Session Data for Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an active user session exists, the system retrieves and loads the session communication area data that was passed from the previous screen. This session data contains user context, navigation history, and program state needed for processing the report request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has navigated to the Transaction Report Request screen and the program communication area is available (session is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is NOT set to TRUE, indicating this is the first time the user has entered this screen in the current session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program proceeds to execute the initial screen display sequence: marking the session as re-entry, clearing screen fields, setting cursor focus, and displaying the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect First Entry and Trigger Initial Screen Setup
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program determines whether the current interaction is the first entry (not a re-entry) by checking the program re-entry flag. If it is the first entry, the initial screen setup sequence is triggered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has confirmed this is the first entry into the Transaction Report Request screen (re-entry flag is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The initial screen setup sequence begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program re-entry flag (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) is set to TRUE so that the next interaction with this screen is recognized as a re-entry and the user's input is processed rather than the screen being re-initialized

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Session as Re-Entry for Subsequent Interactions
all_rules.Rule_Description: Immediately upon first entry, the program marks the session state as a re-entry so that any subsequent return to this screen (e.g., after pressing ENTER) is correctly identified as a re-entry and processed accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has confirmed this is the first entry into the Transaction Report Request screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization sequence is executing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields in the Transaction Report output screen area (CORPT0AO) are set to LOW-VALUES (blank), ensuring no previously displayed data, messages, or field values are visible to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize All Transaction Report Screen Fields to Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: On first entry, all output fields on the Transaction Report screen are cleared to blank (LOW-VALUES) to ensure the user is presented with a clean, empty form with no residual data from any prior session or navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Report screen is being prepared for its initial display to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is about to be sent to the user's terminal for the first time
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor is positioned on the Monthly report option input field (MONTHLYL of CORPT0AI is set to -1), so the user's focus is directed to the first report type selection option

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Cursor Focus to Monthly Report Option Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction Report screen is first displayed, the cursor is automatically positioned on the Monthly report option field, guiding the user to begin their selection from the first available report type option.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All screen fields have been initialized to blank values and the cursor has been positioned on the Monthly report option field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SEND-TRNRPT-SCREEN procedure is performed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Report Request screen (MAP: CORPT0A, MAPSET: CORPT00) is displayed to the user with the ERASE option active (clearing the entire terminal screen before display), the header is populated with the current system date and time, and the system returns control to CICS awaiting the user's next interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display the Transaction Report Request Screen to the User
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all screen fields have been initialized and cursor focus has been set, the Transaction Report Request screen is sent to the user's terminal with the erase option active, fully replacing any previously displayed content, and the system awaits the user's input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has previously been presented with the Transaction Report Request screen and the session communication area indicates the program has been re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the Transaction Report Request screen by pressing a key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system receives and captures all user inputs from the Transaction Report screen (CORPT0A in mapset CORPT00) into the input map area (CORPT0AI), making all entered field values available for subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Receive Transaction Report Screen on Re-Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system receives and captures all user inputs from the transaction report screen only when the user is returning to the screen (re-entry), not on the initial display. This ensures that user-entered data is only processed after the screen has been presented to the user at least once.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Report Request screen and all screen inputs have been received into the input map area (CORPT0AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the report type selection fields in the order: Monthly (MONTHLYI), then Yearly (YEARLYI), then Custom (CUSTOMI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The report type is determined as follows: if MONTHLYI is not spaces and not empty, the report type is 'Monthly'; else if YEARLYI is not spaces and not empty, the report type is 'Yearly'; else if CUSTOMI is not spaces and not empty, the report type is 'Custom'; if none of the three fields contain a value, no report type is selected and the system will require the user to make a selection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Report Type Selection Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system identifies the user's chosen report type by evaluating which of the three report type indicator fields — Monthly, Yearly, or Custom — contains a non-blank, non-empty value. Only one report type should be selected at a time, and the first non-empty field encountered determines the report type to be processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Report Request screen with the Custom report type selected (CUSTOMI is not spaces and not empty) and has entered values in the custom date range fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the custom date range inputs from the received screen data (CORPT0AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the following start date component fields from the screen input: Start Month (SDTMMI of CORPT0AI), Start Day (SDTDDI of CORPT0AI), and Start Year (SDTYYYYI of CORPT0AI), making each field individually available for validation and date assembly

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Custom Report Start Date Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Custom report type is selected, the system captures the three individual components of the custom start date entered by the user: the start month, start day, and start year. These are captured as separate fields and will be subject to individual validation before being assembled into a complete start date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Report Request screen with the Custom report type selected (CUSTOMI is not spaces and not empty) and has entered values in the custom date range fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the custom date range inputs from the received screen data (CORPT0AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the following end date component fields from the screen input: End Month (EDTMMI of CORPT0AI), End Day (EDTDDI of CORPT0AI), and End Year (EDTYYYYI of CORPT0AI), making each field individually available for validation and date assembly

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Custom Report End Date Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Custom report type is selected, the system captures the three individual components of the custom end date entered by the user: the end month, end day, and end year. These are captured as separate fields and will be subject to individual validation before being assembled into a complete end date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Report Request screen and all screen inputs have been received into the input map area (CORPT0AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the received screen inputs
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the value entered in the Confirmation field (CONFIRMI of CORPT0AI), making it available for subsequent confirmation validation; the field value may be 'Y', 'y', 'N', 'n', blank/empty, or any other entered value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Print Confirmation Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system captures the user's confirmation response from the screen. This confirmation field is required before any report job is submitted for printing, and its value determines whether the report submission proceeds, is cancelled, or results in a validation error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Transaction Report Request screen and all inputs including report type selection, custom date range fields, and confirmation field have been captured from the screen (CORPT0AI)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the key pressed by the user (EIBAID)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system routes processing as follows: if the ENTER key (DFHENTER) was pressed, all captured inputs are passed to the Enter Key Processing function (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY) for report type evaluation, date validation, and job submission; if PF3 (DFHPF3) was pressed, the user is navigated to the Main Menu screen (COMEN01C) and captured inputs are not processed further; if any other key was pressed, an error message 'Invalid Key' (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) is displayed, the error flag is set to 'Y', the cursor is repositioned to the Monthly field (MONTHLYL = -1), and the screen is redisplayed without processing the captured inputs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Captured Inputs for Further Processing Based on Key Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all screen inputs are captured, the system routes the processing based on which key the user pressed. Only the ENTER key triggers report processing; PF3 navigates back to the main menu; any other key results in an invalid key error. This routing ensures all captured inputs are directed to the correct processing path.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has previously been presented with the Transaction Report Request screen and has entered data into one or more fields (report type selection, date fields, confirmation field)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen by pressing any key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures and reads all user-entered input data from the Transaction Report Request screen (CORPT0A / CORPT00) into the working input area (CORPT0AI) so that the data is available for subsequent key evaluation and business processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture User Inputs from Transaction Report Request Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits the Transaction Report Request screen, the system must capture all user-entered data from the screen before any processing or key evaluation takes place.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered data on the Transaction Report Request screen and all user inputs have been captured from the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the key pressed and determines it is the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system invokes the report request processing routine (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY) to validate the selected report type, date range inputs, and proceed with report submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route to Report Processing When ENTER Key Is Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the ENTER key on the Transaction Report Request screen, the system must route the request to the report validation and submission process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report Request screen and all user inputs have been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the key pressed and determines it is the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Main Menu (COMEN01C) and transfers control to the Main Menu screen, passing along the current session communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate Back to Main Menu When PF3 Key Is Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the PF3 key on the Transaction Report Request screen, the system must set the navigation destination to the Main Menu and transfer control to it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report Request screen and all user inputs have been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the key pressed and determines it is neither the ENTER key nor the PF3 key (i.e., any other function key or action key)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active ('Y'), positions the cursor on the Monthly report selection field, populates the screen error message area with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the Transaction Report Request screen to the user awaiting the next valid key action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Invalid Key Error Message for Unrecognized Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3 on the Transaction Report Request screen, the system must flag an error, display an invalid key message, and redisplay the screen with the cursor repositioned to the Monthly report field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen and has pressed the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Monthly report type field (MONTHLYI) contains a non-blank, non-empty value indicating the user has selected the Monthly report option
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the report name to 'Monthly' and proceeds to the Monthly Report processing workflow to calculate date ranges and prepare the report for submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Monthly Report Type Selection and Routing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user selects the Monthly report type on the Transaction Report screen, the system recognizes the selection and routes processing to the Monthly report workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen, has pressed the ENTER key, and the Monthly report type field is blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Yearly report type field (YEARLYI) contains a non-blank, non-empty value indicating the user has selected the Yearly report option
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the report name to 'Yearly' and proceeds to the Yearly Report processing workflow to calculate date ranges and prepare the report for submission

all_rules.Rule_Name: Yearly Report Type Selection and Routing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Monthly report type is not selected but the Yearly report type is selected on the Transaction Report screen, the system recognizes the selection and routes processing to the Yearly report workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen, has pressed the ENTER key, and both the Monthly and Yearly report type fields are blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Custom report type field (CUSTOMI) contains a non-blank, non-empty value indicating the user has selected the Custom report option
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the report name to 'Custom' and proceeds to the Custom Report processing workflow, which requires the user to provide a valid start date and end date for the report range

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Report Type Selection and Routing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When neither Monthly nor Yearly report types are selected but the Custom report type is selected on the Transaction Report screen, the system recognizes the selection and routes processing to the Custom report workflow requiring user-entered date ranges.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Transaction Report screen and has pressed the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: None of the three report type fields — Monthly (MONTHLYI), Yearly (YEARLYI), or Custom (CUSTOMI) — contain a non-blank, non-empty value, meaning no report type has been selected
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Select a report type to print report...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Monthly report type field to guide the user, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen with the error message visible

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Report Type Selected — Mandatory Selection Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses ENTER without selecting any report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), the system enforces that a report type selection is mandatory before any report can be submitted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Monthly report type on the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins calculating the date range for the Monthly report
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date, capturing the current Year, current Month, and current Day as the basis for all subsequent date calculations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date for Monthly Report
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Monthly report type is selected, the system must retrieve the current system date to use as the basis for calculating the report's start and end dates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has retrieved the current system date with Year, Month, and Day components
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the start date for the Monthly report
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The start date is set with Year equal to the current system year, Month equal to the current system month, and Day fixed to '01', representing the first day of the current month

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Monthly Report Start Date to First Day of Current Month
all_rules.Rule_Description: The start date for the Monthly report is automatically determined as the first day of the current calendar month, using the current system year and month.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The start date for the Monthly report has been set to the first day of the current month
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the intermediate date needed to derive the end date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the day component to 1 and increments the month component by 1, producing the first day of the next month as an intermediate calculation value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Advance to First Day of Next Month for End Date Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: To determine the last day of the current month, the system first calculates the first day of the next month by advancing the month by 1 and setting the day to 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has advanced the month by 1 as part of the Monthly report end date calculation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The advanced month value is greater than 12 (i.e., the current month is December)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system increments the year by 1 and resets the month to 1 (January), so that the intermediate date correctly represents January 1st of the following year

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle December to January Year Rollover for Monthly Report End Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the current month is December, advancing the month by 1 would produce month 13, which is invalid. The system must roll over to January of the next year.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined the first day of the next month (with year rollover applied if necessary)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the last day of the current month
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system converts the first day of next month to an integer date representation, subtracts 1, and converts back to a calendar date, yielding the correct last day of the current month including proper handling of months with 28, 29, 30, or 31 days

all_rules.Rule_Name: Calculate Last Day of Current Month by Subtracting One Day
all_rules.Rule_Description: The last day of the current month is derived by subtracting exactly one day from the first day of the next month, correctly handling all month-length variations including leap years.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has calculated the last day of the current month
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the end date for the Monthly report
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end date Year is set to the year component of the calculated last day, the end date Month is set to the month component of the calculated last day, and the end date Day is set to the day component of the calculated last day

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Monthly Report End Date from Calculated Last Day
all_rules.Rule_Description: After computing the last day of the current month, the system assigns the resulting year, month, and day components to form the end date of the Monthly report.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Monthly report start date (first day of current month) and end date (last day of current month) have been successfully calculated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the report job for submission
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The calculated start date is stored in both report job start date parameter slots (PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2), and the calculated end date is stored in both report job end date parameter slots (PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2), after which the system proceeds to the job submission confirmation step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Embed Calculated Start and End Dates into Monthly Report Job Parameters
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the start date and end date for the Monthly report have been calculated, both dates must be embedded into the report job parameters before proceeding to job submission.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type on the Transaction Report screen (the Yearly field is not empty and not low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the ENTER key action for the Yearly report type
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and stores it in the working date field (WS-CURDATE-DATA), making the current year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) available for subsequent date range calculations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date for Yearly Report
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Yearly report type is selected, the system must retrieve the current system date in order to determine the current calendar year, which will be used to compute both the start and end dates of the yearly report range.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type and the current system date has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the start date for the Yearly report
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Start Date is set with Month = '01' (January), Day = '01' (1st), and Year = the current calendar year obtained from the system date (WS-CURDATE-YEAR), forming a complete Start Date of YYYY-01-01

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Yearly Report Start Date to January 1st of Current Year
