all_rules.Rule_Description: For a Yearly report, the start date of the reporting period must always be the first day of the current calendar year — January 1st. The year component is derived from the current system date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type and the current system date has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the end date for the Yearly report
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End Date is set with Month = '12' (December), Day = '31' (31st), and Year = the current calendar year obtained from the system date (WS-CURDATE-YEAR), forming a complete End Date of YYYY-12-31

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Yearly Report End Date to December 31st of Current Year
all_rules.Rule_Description: For a Yearly report, the end date of the reporting period must always be the last day of the current calendar year — December 31st. The year component is the same current year used for the start date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Yearly report start date has been calculated as January 1st of the current year (WS-START-DATE = YYYY-01-01)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the report job parameters for submission
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The calculated start date (WS-START-DATE) is stored into both report job start date parameter slots: PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2, ensuring the print job receives the correct start date for the yearly reporting period

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Calculated Yearly Start Date into Report Job Parameters
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the Yearly report start date (January 1st of the current year) has been calculated, it must be stored into the report job submission parameters so that the print job uses the correct reporting period start boundary.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Yearly report end date has been calculated as December 31st of the current year (WS-END-DATE = YYYY-12-31)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the report job parameters for submission
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The calculated end date (WS-END-DATE) is stored into both report job end date parameter slots: PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2, ensuring the print job receives the correct end date for the yearly reporting period

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Calculated Yearly End Date into Report Job Parameters
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the Yearly report end date (December 31st of the current year) has been calculated, it must be stored into the report job submission parameters so that the print job uses the correct reporting period end boundary.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Yearly report type has been selected, the start date (January 1st of current year) and end date (December 31st of current year) have been calculated and stored into the report job parameters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All date calculations and parameter assignments for the Yearly report are complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The report name is set to 'Yearly' and the system proceeds to the report job submission process (SUBMIT-JOB-TO-INTRDR) to initiate the print job submission workflow

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Report Job Submission After Yearly Date Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all Yearly report date parameters have been calculated and stored, the system must set the report name to 'Yearly' and proceed to the report job submission process to queue the print job.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type on the Transaction Report screen and pressed the ENTER key to submit
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Start Date Month field (SDTMM) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'Start Date - Month can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Start Date Month field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Report - Start Month Field Must Not Be Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Custom report type and submits the form, the Start Date Month field must contain a value. If it is left blank, an error message is displayed and the Start Month field is highlighted for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, pressed ENTER, and the Start Date Month field has passed the empty-field validation check
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Start Date Day field (SDTDD) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'Start Date - Day can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Start Date Day field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Report - Start Day Field Must Not Be Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Custom report type and the Start Month field has been validated as populated, the Start Date Day field must also contain a value. If it is left blank, an error message is displayed and the Start Day field is highlighted for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, pressed ENTER, and both the Start Date Month and Start Date Day fields have passed the empty-field validation checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Start Date Year field (SDTYYYY) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'Start Date - Year can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the Start Date Year field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Report - Start Year Field Must Not Be Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Custom report type and both the Start Month and Start Day fields have been validated as populated, the Start Date Year field must also contain a value. If it is left blank, an error message is displayed and the Start Year field is highlighted for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, pressed ENTER, and all three Start Date fields (Month, Day, Year) have passed the empty-field validation checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End Date Month field (EDTMM) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'End Date - Month can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the End Date Month field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Report - End Month Field Must Not Be Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Custom report type and all three Start Date fields have been validated as populated, the End Date Month field must also contain a value. If it is left blank, an error message is displayed and the End Month field is highlighted for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, pressed ENTER, and all three Start Date fields and the End Date Month field have passed the empty-field validation checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End Date Day field (EDTDD) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'End Date - Day can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the End Date Day field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Report - End Day Field Must Not Be Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Custom report type and the Start Date fields plus the End Month field have been validated as populated, the End Date Day field must also contain a value. If it is left blank, an error message is displayed and the End Day field is highlighted for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, pressed ENTER, and all five preceding date fields (Start Month, Start Day, Start Year, End Month, End Day) have passed the empty-field validation checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End Date Year field (EDTYYYY) is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to active, displays the error message 'End Date - Year can NOT be empty...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the End Date Year field to highlight it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen without proceeding further

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Report - End Year Field Must Not Be Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Custom report type and all five preceding date fields have been validated as populated, the End Date Year field must also contain a value. If it is left blank, an error message is displayed and the End Year field is highlighted for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and pressed ENTER to submit the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All six date fields — Start Date Month (SDTMM), Start Date Day (SDTDD), Start Date Year (SDTYYYY), End Date Month (EDTMM), End Date Day (EDTDD), and End Date Year (EDTYYYY) — are all populated with non-blank values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not raise any empty-field error, clears the empty-field validation stage, and advances processing to the numeric and range validation stage for all six date fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Report - All Six Date Fields Populated - Proceed to Numeric Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Custom report type and all six date fields (Start Month, Start Day, Start Year, End Month, End Day, End Year) have been confirmed as non-empty, the system proceeds to the next stage of validation which checks that each field contains a valid numeric value within an acceptable range.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and the Start Month field contains a user-entered text value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins numeric conversion of the custom date fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Start Month input value is converted to its numeric equivalent using a numeric evaluation function and the converted numeric value is stored back into the Start Month field, replacing the original text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Start Month Input to Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validating the custom report Start Month, the system converts the user-entered Start Month text input into a pure numeric value so it can be evaluated against valid month range criteria.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a custom date range and the Start Month field has been converted to a numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Start Month value is numeric AND is less than or equal to 12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Start Month value is NOT numeric OR is greater than 12, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Start Date - Not a valid Month...', highlights the Start Month input field by positioning the cursor on it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; if the Start Month is valid, processing continues to Start Day conversion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Start Month is Numeric and Within Valid Range
all_rules.Rule_Description: After numeric conversion, the system validates that the Start Month value is a proper numeric value and falls within the valid calendar month range of 1 through 12. If either condition fails, an error is raised and the screen is redisplayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and the Start Month has passed numeric validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to convert the Start Day field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Start Day input value is converted to its numeric equivalent using a numeric evaluation function and the converted numeric value is stored back into the Start Day field, replacing the original text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Start Day Input to Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Start Month passes numeric validation, the system converts the user-entered Start Day text input into a pure numeric value so it can be evaluated against valid day range criteria.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a custom date range and the Start Day field has been converted to a numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Start Day value is numeric AND is less than or equal to 31
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Start Day value is NOT numeric OR is greater than 31, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Start Date - Not a valid Day...', highlights the Start Day input field by positioning the cursor on it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; if the Start Day is valid, processing continues to Start Year conversion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Start Day is Numeric and Within Valid Range
all_rules.Rule_Description: After numeric conversion, the system validates that the Start Day value is a proper numeric value and falls within the valid calendar day range of 1 through 31. If either condition fails, an error is raised and the screen is redisplayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and both Start Month and Start Day have passed numeric validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to convert the Start Year field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Start Year input value is converted to its numeric equivalent using a numeric evaluation function and the converted numeric value (up to 4 digits) is stored back into the Start Year field, replacing the original text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Start Year Input to Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Start Day passes numeric validation, the system converts the user-entered Start Year text input into a pure numeric value so it can be evaluated for numeric validity. The Start Year field accepts up to four digits.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a custom date range and the Start Year field has been converted to a numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Start Year value is numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Start Year value is NOT numeric, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Start Date - Not a valid Year...', highlights the Start Year input field by positioning the cursor on it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; if the Start Year is valid, processing continues to End Month conversion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Start Year is Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: After numeric conversion, the system validates that the Start Year value is a proper numeric value. No upper or lower range limit is applied to the year; only numeric integrity is checked.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and all three Start Date fields (Month, Day, Year) have passed numeric validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to convert the End Month field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End Month input value is converted to its numeric equivalent using a numeric evaluation function and the converted numeric value is stored back into the End Month field, replacing the original text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert End Month Input to Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all Start Date fields pass numeric validation, the system converts the user-entered End Month text input into a pure numeric value so it can be evaluated against valid month range criteria.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a custom date range and the End Month field has been converted to a numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the End Month value is numeric AND is less than or equal to 12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the End Month value is NOT numeric OR is greater than 12, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'End Date - Not a valid Month...', highlights the End Month input field by positioning the cursor on it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; if the End Month is valid, processing continues to End Day conversion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate End Month is Numeric and Within Valid Range
all_rules.Rule_Description: After numeric conversion, the system validates that the End Month value is a proper numeric value and falls within the valid calendar month range of 1 through 12. If either condition fails, an error is raised and the screen is redisplayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and the End Month has passed numeric validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to convert the End Day field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End Day input value is converted to its numeric equivalent using a numeric evaluation function and the converted numeric value is stored back into the End Day field, replacing the original text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert End Day Input to Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the End Month passes numeric validation, the system converts the user-entered End Day text input into a pure numeric value so it can be evaluated against valid day range criteria.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a custom date range and the End Day field has been converted to a numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the End Day value is numeric AND is less than or equal to 31
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the End Day value is NOT numeric OR is greater than 31, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'End Date - Not a valid Day...', highlights the End Day input field by positioning the cursor on it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; if the End Day is valid, processing continues to End Year conversion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate End Day is Numeric and Within Valid Range
all_rules.Rule_Description: After numeric conversion, the system validates that the End Day value is a proper numeric value and falls within the valid calendar day range of 1 through 31. If either condition fails, an error is raised and the screen is redisplayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type, all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and both End Month and End Day have passed numeric validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to convert the End Year field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End Year input value is converted to its numeric equivalent using a numeric evaluation function and the converted numeric value (up to 4 digits) is stored back into the End Year field, replacing the original text input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert End Year Input to Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the End Day passes numeric validation, the system converts the user-entered End Year text input into a pure numeric value so it can be evaluated for numeric validity. The End Year field accepts up to four digits.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a custom date range and the End Year field has been converted to a numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the End Year value is numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the End Year value is NOT numeric, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'End Date - Not a valid Year...', highlights the End Year input field by positioning the cursor on it, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; if the End Year is valid, all six custom date fields are confirmed as numeric and processing advances to calendar date range validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate End Year is Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: After numeric conversion, the system validates that the End Year value is a proper numeric value. No upper or lower range limit is applied to the year; only numeric integrity is checked. Successful validation means all six custom date fields are confirmed numeric and processing advances to range validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Custom report type and has entered values in the custom date range fields, and the Start Date Month field has been converted to its numeric equivalent
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses ENTER and the system evaluates the Start Date Month field, and the Start Month value is either non-numeric OR is greater than 12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Start Date - Not a valid Month...' on the screen, highlights (positions cursor on) the Start Month field, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; processing continues to evaluate the remaining date fields regardless of this error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Custom Report Start Month Does Not Exceed Maximum Allowed Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a custom date range for a transaction report, the Start Date Month must be a valid numeric value and must not exceed 12 (the maximum number of months in a year). If the value is non-numeric or greater than 12, an error message is displayed and the Start Month field is highlighted for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Custom report type and has entered values in the custom date range fields, and the Start Date Day field has been converted to its numeric equivalent
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses ENTER and the system evaluates the Start Date Day field, and the Start Day value is either non-numeric OR is greater than 31
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Start Date - Not a valid Day...' on the screen, highlights (positions cursor on) the Start Day field, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; processing continues to evaluate the remaining date fields regardless of this error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Custom Report Start Day Does Not Exceed Maximum Allowed Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a custom date range for a transaction report, the Start Date Day must be a valid numeric value and must not exceed 31 (the maximum number of days in any month). If the value is non-numeric or greater than 31, an error message is displayed and the Start Day field is highlighted for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Custom report type and has entered values in the custom date range fields, and the End Date Month field has been converted to its numeric equivalent
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses ENTER and the system evaluates the End Date Month field, and the End Month value is either non-numeric OR is greater than 12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'End Date - Not a valid Month...' on the screen, highlights (positions cursor on) the End Month field, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; processing continues to evaluate the remaining date fields regardless of this error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Custom Report End Month Does Not Exceed Maximum Allowed Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a custom date range for a transaction report, the End Date Month must be a valid numeric value and must not exceed 12 (the maximum number of months in a year). If the value is non-numeric or greater than 12, an error message is displayed and the End Month field is highlighted for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Custom report type and has entered values in the custom date range fields, and the End Date Day field has been converted to its numeric equivalent
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses ENTER and the system evaluates the End Date Day field, and the End Day value is either non-numeric OR is greater than 31
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'End Date - Not a valid Day...' on the screen, highlights (positions cursor on) the End Day field, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen; processing continues to evaluate the remaining date fields regardless of this error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Custom Report End Day Does Not Exceed Maximum Allowed Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a custom date range for a transaction report, the End Date Day must be a valid numeric value and must not exceed 31 (the maximum number of days in any month). If the value is non-numeric or greater than 31, an error message is displayed and the End Day field is highlighted for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Custom report type, all six date fields have passed the empty-field check, and all date fields have been successfully converted to numeric values
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates all range conditions and finds that Start Month is numeric and not greater than 12, Start Day is numeric and not greater than 31, End Month is numeric and not greater than 12, and End Day is numeric and not greater than 31
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No range validation error messages are displayed, the error flag remains unset for range validation, and the system proceeds to validate whether the Start Date and End Date represent real existing calendar dates

all_rules.Rule_Name: All Custom Date Range Field Values Pass Range Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all four range-validated date fields (Start Month, Start Day, End Month, End Day) contain values within their permitted numeric ranges, the range validation phase is considered complete and processing advances to the next stage of custom date validation (calendar date validity check).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has selected the Custom report type and has provided values for the Start Date fields (Year, Month, Day) that have passed numeric and range validations, and the start date has been assembled into YYYY-MM-DD format
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the start date (WS-START-DATE) and the date format (WS-DATE-FORMAT) as input parameters and invokes the external CSUTLDTC date validation utility
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The CSUTLDTC utility is called with the assembled start date and date format, and the validation result (including severity code and message number) is returned for further evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke Date Validation Utility for Custom Start Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects the Custom report type and provides a start date, the system must invoke the CSUTLDTC date validation utility by preparing the start date in YYYY-MM-DD format along with the expected date format, then calling the utility to determine whether the date is a real calendar date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CSUTLDTC date validation utility has been called with the custom start date and date format
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The utility returns a severity code equal to '0000', indicating the start date is a valid calendar date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The start date is accepted as valid and processing continues to the end date calendar validity check without any error message or screen redisplay

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept Custom Start Date When Validation Utility Returns Success
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the CSUTLDTC date validation utility is called for the custom start date, if the utility returns a severity code of '0000', the start date is confirmed as a valid calendar date and processing continues to the end date validation step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CSUTLDTC date validation utility has been called with the custom start date and has returned a severity code other than '0000'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message number returned by the utility is '2513', indicating a known acceptable exception
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The start date is treated as valid despite the non-success severity code, no error message is displayed, and processing continues to the end date calendar validity check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Treat Known Validation Exception as Valid for Custom Start Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the CSUTLDTC utility returns a non-success severity code for the custom start date, the system checks whether the returned message number is '2513', which represents a known and acceptable exception. If so, the date is treated as valid and processing continues.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CSUTLDTC date validation utility has been called with the custom start date, has returned a severity code other than '0000', and the returned message number is NOT '2513'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the start date is a genuinely invalid calendar date (e.g., February 30, April 31)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message 'Start Date - Not a valid date...' is set, the error flag is activated, the Start Date Month field is highlighted on the screen (cursor positioned to it), and the Transaction Report screen is redisplayed showing the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Custom Start Date When It Is Not a Real Calendar Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the CSUTLDTC utility returns a non-success severity code for the custom start date and the message number is not the known exception '2513', the start date is determined to be a genuinely invalid calendar date. The system must display an error message, highlight the start date month field, and redisplay the Transaction Report screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and has entered values for End Date Year (EDTYYYYI), End Date Month (EDTMMI), and End Date Day (EDTDDI) on the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the end date for calendar validation after all numeric range checks have passed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system assembles the end date by moving the user-entered End Date Year into WS-END-DATE-YYYY, End Date Month into WS-END-DATE-MM, and End Date Day into WS-END-DATE-DD, forming a complete date value (WS-END-DATE) in YYYY-MM-DD format, which is then loaded into the date validation input field (CSUTLDTC-DATE) along with the expected date format (CSUTLDTC-DATE-FORMAT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom End Date - Prepare Date for Calendar Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validating the custom end date against the calendar, the system assembles the user-entered year, month, and day components into a single end date value in YYYY-MM-DD format, ready for submission to the date validation utility.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The custom end date has been assembled in YYYY-MM-DD format and loaded into CSUTLDTC-DATE, and the date format has been loaded into CSUTLDTC-DATE-FORMAT, and the result area (CSUTLDTC-RESULT) has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calls the CSUTLDTC date validation utility passing the end date (CSUTLDTC-DATE), the date format (CSUTLDTC-DATE-FORMAT), and the result area (CSUTLDTC-RESULT)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The CSUTLDTC utility processes the end date and populates CSUTLDTC-RESULT with a severity code (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD) and a message number (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM) indicating whether the end date is a valid calendar date

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom End Date - Invoke Calendar Date Validation Utility
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system invokes the external date validation utility CSUTLDTC to determine whether the user-entered custom end date represents a real, existing calendar date. This utility receives the assembled end date and its expected format, and returns a validation result including a severity code and message number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CSUTLDTC date validation utility has been called and has returned a result containing a severity code (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD) and a message number (CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM) for the custom end date
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the severity code returned by the CSUTLDTC utility
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the severity code equals '0000', the end date is considered a valid calendar date and processing continues to the next step; if the severity code is anything other than '0000' AND the message number is NOT '2513', the end date is considered invalid and the system sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y', sets the error message to 'End Date - Not a valid date...', highlights the End Date Month field (EDTMML) with cursor positioning (-1), and redisplays the Transaction Report screen with the error; if the severity code is not '0000' but the message number IS '2513', no error is raised and processing continues

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom End Date - Evaluate Calendar Validity Result
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the date validation utility returns its result, the system evaluates the severity code to determine whether the custom end date is a real calendar date. A severity code of '0000' indicates the date is valid. Any other severity code, except for message number '2513', indicates the date is not a valid calendar date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CSUTLDTC date validation utility has returned a severity code other than '0000' AND a message number other than '2513' for the custom end date entered by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the custom end date is not a real calendar date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error message (WS-MESSAGE) to 'End Date - Not a valid date...', sets the error flag (WS-ERR-FLG) to 'Y' to indicate an error condition, positions the cursor on the End Date Month field (EDTMML set to -1) to highlight the error location, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen showing the error message so the user can correct the end date entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom End Date - Display Calendar Validation Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the custom end date fails calendar validation (i.e., the date does not exist in the real calendar, such as February 30), the system informs the user with a specific error message and highlights the End Date Month field to guide the user to correct the invalid date entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a valid report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), all required date validations have passed, and the system is ready to submit the report job for printing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses ENTER and the Confirmation field is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Build a confirmation prompt message dynamically in the format 'Please confirm to print the [Report Name] report...' where [Report Name] is one of 'Monthly', 'Yearly', or 'Custom' based on the selected report type; (2) Set the error indicator to active ('Y'); (3) Position the cursor focus on the Confirmation field; (4) Redisplay the Transaction Report screen showing the confirmation prompt message — the user must then enter a confirmation value and press ENTER again to proceed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirmation Field Empty — Prompt User to Confirm Report Printing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before submitting a report job for printing, the system checks whether the user has provided a value in the Confirmation field. If the field is empty, the system builds a dynamic confirmation prompt message that includes the selected report type name, sets focus on the Confirmation field, and redisplays the Transaction Report screen to prompt the user for an explicit confirmation response.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), all required date validations have passed, and the Confirmation field is displayed prompting the user to confirm the print request
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters 'Y' (uppercase) or 'y' (lowercase) in the Confirmation field and presses ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system accepts the confirmation as valid and proceeds to submit the report batch job to the print queue without displaying any error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed with Report Job Submission on Positive Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters 'Y' or 'y' in the Confirmation field, the system accepts the confirmation as valid and proceeds to submit the report batch job for printing without any error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), all required date validations have passed, and the Confirmation field is displayed prompting the user to confirm the print request
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters 'N' (uppercase) or 'n' (lowercase) in the Confirmation field and presses ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system cancels the report print request; clears all input fields including Monthly, Yearly, Custom selection fields, Start Date (Month, Day, Year), End Date (Month, Day, Year), and Confirmation field; resets the cursor to the Monthly field; and redisplays the screen in its initial cleared state with no success or error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cancel Report Request on Negative Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters 'N' or 'n' in the Confirmation field, the system cancels the report print request, clears all input fields on the screen, and resets the screen to its initial state without submitting any job.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected a report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), all required date validations have passed, and the Confirmation field is displayed prompting the user to confirm the print request
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user enters any value other than 'Y', 'y', 'N', or 'n' in the Confirmation field and presses ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system rejects the confirmation input; constructs and displays the error message in the format: '"[entered value]" is not a valid value to confirm...' where [entered value] is the actual text entered by the user; highlights and positions the cursor on the Confirmation field; and redisplays the Transaction Report screen so the user can provide a valid confirmation value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Invalid Confirmation Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters any value other than 'Y', 'y', 'N', or 'n' in the Confirmation field, the system rejects the input, displays a specific error message identifying the invalid value, highlights the Confirmation field, and redisplays the screen for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Monthly report type on the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Monthly report request and retrieves the current system date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The start date is automatically set to the first day of the current month, formatted as YYYY-MM-01, where YYYY is the current year and MM is the current month (e.g., if today is June 15 2024, the start date is set to 2024-06-01)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Monthly Report Start Date Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Monthly report type is selected, the system automatically calculates the start date as the first day of the current calendar month using the current system date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Monthly report type and the system has determined the current year and month
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the end date for the monthly report
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end date is automatically computed as the last day of the current month using the following logic: (1) Set day to 1, (2) Add 1 to the current month; if the resulting month exceeds 12, increment the year by 1 and reset the month to 1, (3) Convert the resulting first-day-of-next-month date to an integer, subtract 1, and convert back to a calendar date to obtain the last day of the current month, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., if current month is June 2024, end date is set to 2024-06-30)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Monthly Report End Date Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Monthly report type is selected, the system automatically calculates the end date as the last day of the current calendar month by advancing to the first day of the next month and subtracting one day.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type on the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Yearly report request and retrieves the current system date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The start date is automatically set to January 1st of the current year, formatted as YYYY-01-01, where YYYY is the current year (e.g., if today is June 15 2024, the start date is set to 2024-01-01)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Yearly Report Start Date Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Yearly report type is selected, the system automatically sets the start date to January 1st of the current calendar year.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type on the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Yearly report request and retrieves the current system date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end date is automatically set to December 31st of the current year, formatted as YYYY-12-31, where YYYY is the current year (e.g., if today is June 15 2024, the end date is set to 2024-12-31)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Yearly Report End Date Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Yearly report type is selected, the system automatically sets the end date to December 31st of the current calendar year.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and has entered valid values for the start date fields: Start Year (SDTYYYYI), Start Month (SDTMMI), and Start Day (SDTDDI), all of which have passed all empty-field, numeric, range, and calendar validity checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assembles the custom report start date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The start date is constructed by combining the user-entered Start Year into WS-START-DATE-YYYY, Start Month into WS-START-DATE-MM, and Start Day into WS-START-DATE-DD, resulting in a complete start date in YYYY-MM-DD format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Report Start Date Assignment from User Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Custom report type is selected, the system uses the user-entered and validated start date fields (year, month, day) to construct the start date for the report.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type and has entered valid values for the end date fields: End Year (EDTYYYYI), End Month (EDTMMI), and End Day (EDTDDI), all of which have passed all empty-field, numeric, range, and calendar validity checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assembles the custom report end date
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end date is constructed by combining the user-entered End Year into WS-END-DATE-YYYY, End Month into WS-END-DATE-MM, and End Day into WS-END-DATE-DD, resulting in a complete end date in YYYY-MM-DD format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Custom Report End Date Assignment from User Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Custom report type is selected, the system uses the user-entered and validated end date fields (year, month, day) to construct the end date for the report.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom) has been selected and the corresponding start date has been determined — either calculated by the system (Monthly/Yearly) or entered and validated by the user (Custom)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the JCL records for batch job submission
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The start date value (WS-START-DATE in YYYY-MM-DD format) is copied into both JCL parameter fields PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2, so that the batch job receives the correct start date of the reporting period in both parameter positions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Embed Start Date into JCL Parameter Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of the report type selected (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), the calculated or validated start date must be embedded into both JCL start date parameter fields (PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2) to ensure the batch job uses the correct reporting period start date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom) has been selected and the corresponding end date has been determined — either calculated by the system (Monthly/Yearly) or entered and validated by the user (Custom)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the JCL records for batch job submission
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end date value (WS-END-DATE in YYYY-MM-DD format) is copied into both JCL parameter fields PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2, so that the batch job receives the correct end date of the reporting period in both parameter positions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Embed End Date into JCL Parameter Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of the report type selected (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), the calculated or validated end date must be embedded into both JCL end date parameter fields (PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2) to ensure the batch job uses the correct reporting period end date.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The start date has been embedded into PARM-START-DATE-1 and PARM-START-DATE-2, and the end date has been embedded into PARM-END-DATE-1 and PARM-END-DATE-2 for the selected report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All date parameters have been successfully populated in the JCL records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The JCL records are considered fully prepared with the correct date parameters and the process proceeds to the job submission step, where the JCL records will be written to the JOBS transient data queue (internal reader) for batch execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: JCL Records Ready for Job Submission After Date Embedding
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once both the start and end dates have been embedded into all four JCL parameter fields, the JCL records are considered complete and ready to be submitted to the internal job reader queue for batch processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the Transaction Report screen with a report type selected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the selected report type to determine the date source for JCL parameter construction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system applies the following decision: (1) If Monthly is selected — use system-calculated dates (first and last day of current month); (2) If Yearly is selected — use system-calculated dates (January 1st and December 31st of current year); (3) If Custom is selected — use the user-entered and fully validated start and end dates; in all cases, the determined dates are then embedded into the JCL parameter fields PARM-START-DATE-1, PARM-START-DATE-2, PARM-END-DATE-1, and PARM-END-DATE-2

all_rules.Rule_Name: Report Type Determines Date Source for JCL Construction
all_rules.Rule_Description: The source of the start and end dates used in JCL construction is determined by the report type selected by the user: Monthly and Yearly report types use system-calculated dates, while the Custom report type uses user-entered and validated dates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has confirmed the report submission with 'Y' or 'y' in the confirmation field and no prior errors exist
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the batch job submission process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system initializes the JCL record processing starting from the first record (index position 1) in the job definition list, with the end-of-loop indicator set to 'No' so that processing can begin

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Batch Job Submission Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a report job is confirmed for submission, the system initializes the JCL record processing by starting from the very first record in the job definition list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The batch job submission process is actively writing JCL records to the JOBS queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether more records remain to be processed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system continues processing only if the current record index is 1000 or fewer AND the end-of-loop indicator is 'No' AND no errors have occurred; if the record index exceeds 1000, processing stops and the job submission is considered complete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enforce Maximum JCL Record Processing Limit
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system enforces a maximum limit of 1000 JCL records that can be processed during a single batch job submission to prevent runaway processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The batch job submission loop is active, the record count is within the 1000-record limit, no end-of-file condition has been set, and no errors have occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the next JCL record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the JCL record at the current index position from the job lines collection (JOB-LINES) and loads it into the active JCL record buffer (JCL-RECORD) for further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next JCL Record from Job Definition
all_rules.Rule_Description: During batch job submission, the system sequentially reads each JCL record from the job definition list using the current index position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A JCL record has been read from the job definition list into the active record buffer
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the content of the current JCL record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the record contains the end-of-file marker '/*EOF', or the record contains only spaces, or the record contains only low-values (empty binary content), the system sets the end-of-loop indicator to 'Yes' to stop further processing; otherwise, the record is treated as a valid JCL record and submitted to the queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect End-of-Job Marker or Blank Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: After reading each JCL record, the system checks whether the record signals the end of the job definition, either through an explicit end-of-file marker or by being blank/empty.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The batch job submission loop is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either the current JCL record is an EOF marker ('/*EOF') or blank/empty, OR the record index has exceeded 1000 records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system exits the JCL record processing loop and proceeds to finalize the job submission, with no further records written to the JOBS queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop JCL Record Processing on End-of-File or Limit Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system terminates JCL record processing when either an end-of-file condition is detected or the maximum record limit of 1000 has been reached, signaling that the job submission sequence is complete.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid JCL record has been read (not an EOF marker and not blank/empty) and the record index is within the 1000-record limit
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system submits the current JCL record to the batch job queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system writes the JCL record from the active record buffer (JCL-RECORD) to the JOBS transient data queue with the full record length, making it available to the internal reader for batch job execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write JCL Record to JOBS Internal Reader Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each valid JCL record is written to the JOBS transient data queue, which acts as the internal reader to trigger batch job execution for the transaction report.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write a JCL record to the JOBS transient data queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The write operation does not complete successfully (response code is not NORMAL)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Unable to Write TDQ (JOBS)...' on the report screen, positions the cursor on the Monthly field, and stops further JCL record processing; the batch job is not submitted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Failure to Write JCL Record to JOBS Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the system fails to write a JCL record to the JOBS internal reader queue, an error is raised, the submission is halted, and the user is notified that the job could not be submitted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A JCL record has been successfully written to the JOBS transient data queue with a NORMAL response
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the write was successful
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system increments the record index by 1 and returns to check whether more records remain to be processed, continuing the sequential submission of JCL records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Write and Advance to Next JCL Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a JCL record is successfully written to the JOBS queue, the system advances the record index to process the next record in sequence.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All JCL records up to the EOF marker or the 1000-record limit have been processed and written to the JOBS queue with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The batch job submission loop exits normally
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system considers the job submission complete; control returns to the calling process (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY), which then clears all input fields, displays a success message in green reading '[Report Name] report submitted for printing ...' on the transaction report screen, and repositions the cursor on the Monthly field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Complete Batch Job Submission
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all JCL records have been written to the JOBS queue without errors, the batch job submission is considered complete and control returns to the report screen with a success confirmation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has completed the report submission process by selecting a report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom), providing valid inputs, confirming the submission, and the system has attempted to write the job to the print queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether any errors were flagged during the entire submission process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If and only if no errors were detected (error flag is OFF), the system proceeds to clear all input fields, set the success message color to green, build the success message, and display the Transaction Report screen with the success notification; if any errors were detected, the success notification is suppressed and the screen remains in its error state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Success Notification Only When No Errors Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the job submission process completes, the success notification flow is only triggered if no errors were encountered during the entire report submission process (report type selection, date validation, confirmation, and job queue writing).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The job submission has completed successfully with no errors detected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the success notification sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears and resets all of the following input fields to their initial empty values: Monthly selector (MONTHLYI), Yearly selector (YEARLYI), Custom selector (CUSTOMI), Start Date Month (SDTMMI), Start Date Day (SDTDDI), Start Date Year (SDTYYYYI), End Date Month (EDTMMI), End Date Day (EDTDDI), End Date Year (EDTYYYYI), Confirmation field (CONFIRMI), and the on-screen message area (WS-MESSAGE); additionally, the cursor position is set to the Monthly field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Input Fields After Successful Job Submission
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful job submission with no errors, all user input fields on the Transaction Report screen are reset to their initial empty state, including report type selectors, all custom date fields, and the confirmation field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The job submission has completed successfully with no errors detected and all input fields have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the success notification message for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the message display color attribute for the error/message area (ERRMSGC) on the Transaction Report screen output (CORPT0AO) to green (DFHGREEN), so that the success message is rendered in green text on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Success Message Display Color to Green
all_rules.Rule_Description: The success confirmation message is visually distinguished from error messages by displaying it in green color on the Transaction Report screen, providing a clear positive visual indicator to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Monthly report type (MONTHLYI field on the screen is not spaces and not low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Enter key action and identifies the selected report type
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system assigns the value 'Monthly' to the report name variable (WS-REPORT-NAME), which will be used to construct the success message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Report Name 'Monthly' for Monthly Report Type
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user selects the Monthly report option, the internal report name is set to 'Monthly', which is subsequently used to build the success confirmation message displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Yearly report type (YEARLYI field on the screen is not spaces and not low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Enter key action and identifies the selected report type
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system assigns the value 'Yearly' to the report name variable (WS-REPORT-NAME), which will be used to construct the success message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Report Name 'Yearly' for Yearly Report Type
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user selects the Yearly report option, the internal report name is set to 'Yearly', which is subsequently used to build the success confirmation message displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected the Custom report type (CUSTOMI field on the screen is not spaces and not low-values) and all custom date validations have passed with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Enter key action and identifies the selected report type
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system assigns the value 'Custom' to the report name variable (WS-REPORT-NAME), which will be used to construct the success message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Report Name 'Custom' for Custom Date Range Report Type
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user selects the Custom date range report option, the internal report name is set to 'Custom', which is subsequently used to build the success confirmation message displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The job submission has completed successfully with no errors, all input fields have been cleared, the message color has been set to green, and the report name variable (WS-REPORT-NAME) contains the value 'Monthly', 'Yearly', or 'Custom' based on the report type selected by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the success notification message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system constructs the message by concatenating the report name (WS-REPORT-NAME, trimmed of trailing spaces) with the fixed text ' report submitted for printing ...' and stores the result in the message field (WS-MESSAGE); the resulting messages are: 'Monthly report submitted for printing ...', 'Yearly report submitted for printing ...', or 'Custom report submitted for printing ...' respectively

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Dynamic Success Message Based on Submitted Report Type
all_rules.Rule_Description: The success confirmation message is dynamically constructed by combining the report type name with a standard confirmation phrase, resulting in a report-type-specific message such as 'Monthly report submitted for printing...', 'Yearly report submitted for printing...', or 'Custom report submitted for printing...'

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All input fields have been cleared, the message color has been set to green, and the success message has been built indicating which report type was submitted for printing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Transaction Report screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the cursor position to the Monthly field (MONTHLYL of CORPT0AI set to -1), populates the screen header with the current date and time, moves the success message (WS-MESSAGE) to the screen message area (ERRMSGO of CORPT0AO), and displays the Transaction Report screen (map CORPT0A from mapset CORPT00) with the green success message and cursor on the Monthly field; the system then returns control to CICS awaiting the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Transaction Report Screen with Green Success Message and Cursor on Monthly Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: After building the success message, the Transaction Report screen is refreshed and displayed to the user showing the green success confirmation message, with the cursor automatically positioned on the Monthly report selector field, ready for the user's next action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Report screen is about to be displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores them in the working date/time data area (WS-CURDATE-DATA), making the current month, day, year, hours, minutes, and seconds available for subsequent header field population

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen header, the system retrieves the current system date and time to ensure all header information reflects the real-time values at the moment of screen display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and the application title constants (CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02) are defined in the common application data area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The application title fields are being set on the Transaction Report screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed into the Title Line 1 output field (TITLE01O) of the screen, and Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed into the Title Line 2 output field (TITLE02O) of the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Application Title Lines on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display the standard application title lines sourced from the centrally defined application title constants, ensuring consistent branding across all screens.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is available in the working storage
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction identifier field is being set on the Transaction Report screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is placed into the Transaction Name output field (TRNNAMEO) of the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Transaction ID on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display the current transaction identifier so that users and support staff can identify which transaction is active on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is available in the working storage
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program name field is being set on the Transaction Report screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is placed into the Program Name output field (PGMNAMEO) of the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Program Name on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display the name of the currently executing program so that users and support staff can identify which program is serving the current screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and the month (WS-CURDATE-MONTH), day (WS-CURDATE-DAY), and four-digit year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) components are available in working storage
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The date field is being formatted and set on the Transaction Report screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current month is moved to the MM portion of the display date (WS-CURDATE-MM), the current day is moved to the DD portion (WS-CURDATE-DD), only the last two digits of the current year (positions 3 and 4 of WS-CURDATE-YEAR) are moved to the YY portion (WS-CURDATE-YY), and the fully assembled MM/DD/YY formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) is placed into the Current Date output field (CURDATEO) of the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Date as MM/DD/YY on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current date displayed on the screen header must be formatted in MM/DD/YY format, using only the last two digits of the year, to provide a concise and standardized date reference for the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and the hours (WS-CURTIME-HOURS), minutes (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE), and seconds (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) components are available in working storage
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The time field is being formatted and set on the Transaction Report screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current hours are moved to the HH portion of the display time (WS-CURTIME-HH), the current minutes are moved to the MM portion (WS-CURTIME-MM), the current seconds are moved to the SS portion (WS-CURTIME-SS), and the fully assembled HH:MM:SS formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) is placed into the Current Time output field (CURTIMEO) of the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Time as HH:MM:SS on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current time displayed on the screen header must be formatted in HH:MM:SS format, providing hours, minutes, and seconds to give users an accurate real-time reference at the moment the screen is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has triggered an All Fields Initialization event, either following a successful report job submission or when the user cancels a report submission by entering 'N' in the confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The initialization routine executes the reset of report type selector fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Monthly report selector field (MONTHLYI) is reset to its default empty state, the Yearly report selector field (YEARLYI) is reset to its default empty state, and the Custom report selector field (CUSTOMI) is reset to its default empty state — ensuring no report type remains pre-selected on the refreshed screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Report Type Selectors During Field Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen fields are initialized (either after a successful report submission or when the user cancels a submission), all three report type selector fields — Monthly, Yearly, and Custom — must be cleared to their empty/default state so the user starts with a clean selection.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has triggered an All Fields Initialization event, either following a successful report job submission or when the user cancels a report submission by entering 'N' in the confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The initialization routine executes the reset of Start Date input fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Start Date Month field (SDTMMI) is reset to its default empty state, the Start Date Day field (SDTDDI) is reset to its default empty state, and the Start Date Year field (SDTYYYYI) is reset to its default empty state — ensuring no previously entered start date values persist on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Start Date Fields During Field Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen fields are initialized, all three components of the custom report Start Date — Month, Day, and Year — must be cleared to their empty/default state so no previously entered start date values remain visible on the refreshed screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has triggered an All Fields Initialization event, either following a successful report job submission or when the user cancels a report submission by entering 'N' in the confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The initialization routine executes the reset of End Date input fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End Date Month field (EDTMMI) is reset to its default empty state, the End Date Day field (EDTDDI) is reset to its default empty state, and the End Date Year field (EDTYYYYI) is reset to its default empty state — ensuring no previously entered end date values persist on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset End Date Fields During Field Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen fields are initialized, all three components of the custom report End Date — Month, Day, and Year — must be cleared to their empty/default state so no previously entered end date values remain visible on the refreshed screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has triggered an All Fields Initialization event, either following a successful report job submission or when the user cancels a report submission by entering 'N' in the confirmation field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The initialization routine executes the reset of the confirmation and message fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The print confirmation input field (CONFIRMI) is reset to its default empty state, and the screen message area (WS-MESSAGE) is reset to its default empty state — ensuring no prior confirmation value or informational/error message remains visible to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Confirmation and Message Fields During Field Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen fields are initialized, the print confirmation field and the screen message area must both be cleared to their empty/default state, ensuring no prior confirmation input or status message remains displayed on the refreshed screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed resetting all screen input fields — report type selectors, start date fields, end date fields, confirmation field, and message area — as part of the All Fields Initialization routine
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The initialization routine sets the cursor position for the refreshed screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor focus is set to the Monthly report selector field (MONTHLYL is set to -1), so that when the Transaction Report screen is next displayed, the cursor is automatically positioned on the Monthly field, ready for the user's next report type selection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Cursor Focus to Monthly Report Field After Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all screen fields have been initialized/reset, the screen cursor must be automatically positioned on the Monthly report selector field. This guides the user to begin their next report selection from the first available report type option.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The navigation to a previous screen has been initiated and the target program field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) in the communication area contains LOW-VALUES or SPACES, indicating no destination has been specified
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the target program field before transferring control
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The target program is set to the Sign-On screen identifier 'COSGN00C' so that navigation proceeds to a valid default destination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Target Screen When No Destination Is Specified
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigation to a previous screen is triggered but no target screen has been set in the communication area, the system defaults the destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to navigate away from the Transaction Report screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The navigation procedure is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is recorded as the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) in the shared communication area passed to the destination screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Originating Transaction ID Before Navigation

description:
CORPT00C is a CICS online program within the CardDemo application that allows users to generate and submit transaction reports by writing JCL job records to an extra-partition Transient Data Queue (TDQ). The program supports three report types — Monthly, Yearly, and Custom date range — and validates user-entered date inputs before submitting the batch job to the internal reader (JOBS TDQ) for execution.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: None (No VSAM, DB2, or IMS) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Entry and Session Validation - Check if the program is being called for the first time (EIBCALEN = 0). If no communication area exists, redirect the user to the sign-on screen. Otherwise, load the existing communication area for processing. 2: Initial Screen Display - On the first entry into the program (not a re-entry), initialize the transaction report screen with blank fields and display it to the user, setting cursor focus on the Monthly report option. 3: Screen Input Reception - Receive and capture all user inputs from the transaction report request screen, including report type selection (Monthly, Yearly, Custom) and date range fields. 4: User Key Action Handling - Evaluate which key the user pressed. If Enter, process the report request. If PF3, navigate back to the main menu (COMEN01C). If any other key, display an invalid key error message and redisplay the screen. 5: Report Type Selection Validation - Validate that the user has selected at least one report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom). If none is selected, display an error message prompting the user to select a report type. 6: Monthly Report Date Calculation - When the Monthly report type is selected, automatically calculate the start date as the first day of the current month and the end date as the last day of the current month using the system current date. 7: Yearly Report Date Calculation - When the Yearly report type is selected, automatically set the start date to January 1st of the current year and the end date to December 31st of the current year. 8: Custom Date Range - Empty Field Validation - When the Custom report type is selected, validate that all six date fields (Start Month, Start Day, Start Year, End Month, End Day, End Year) are not empty. Display a specific error message for each missing field and highlight the offending field. 9: Custom Date Range - Numeric Field Validation - Convert and validate that all custom date input fields (Start Month, Start Day, Start Year, End Month, End Day, End Year) contain valid numeric values. 10: Custom Date Range - Range Validation - Validate that the Start Month and End Month are not greater than 12, and that the Start Day and End Day are not greater than 31. Display appropriate error messages for invalid values. 11: Custom Start Date - Calendar Validity Check - Validate the custom start date (YYYY-MM-DD) is a real calendar date by calling the CSUTLDTC date validation utility. If the date is invalid, display an error message and highlight the start date month field. 12: Custom End Date - Calendar Validity Check - Validate the custom end date (YYYY-MM-DD) is a real calendar date by calling the CSUTLDTC date validation utility. If the date is invalid, display an error message and highlight the end date month field. 13: Report Submission Confirmation Request - Before submitting the report job, check if the user has entered a confirmation value. If the confirmation field is empty, prompt the user to confirm by displaying a message asking them to confirm printing of the selected report type. 14: Confirmation Value Validation - Validate the user's confirmation input. If 'Y' or 'y', proceed with job submission. If 'N' or 'n', cancel the request, clear all fields, and redisplay the screen. If any other value, display an error indicating the value is not valid for confirmation. 15: Batch Job JCL Construction - Prepare the JCL (Job Control Language) records for the transaction report batch job, embedding the calculated or user-entered start and end dates into the appropriate JCL parameter fields (PARM-START-DATE and PARM-END-DATE). 16: Batch Job Submission to Internal Reader - Write each JCL record line-by-line to the JOBS transient data queue (TDQ), which acts as an internal reader to submit the batch transaction report job for execution. Stop writing when the end-of-file marker or blank record is encountered. 17: Job Submission Success Notification - After successful job submission, clear all input fields, set the message color to green, and display a success confirmation message indicating which report type (Monthly, Yearly, or Custom) has been submitted for printing. 18: Screen Header Population - Populate the screen header with application title lines, current transaction ID, program name, current date (MM/DD/YY format), and current time (HH:MM:SS format) before every screen display. 19: All Fields Initialization - Reset all screen input fields (Monthly, Yearly, Custom selectors, all date fields, confirmation field) and the message area to their initial empty state, and set cursor focus to the Monthly field. 20: Navigation to Previous Screen - Transfer control back to the previous screen or the main menu, passing along the communication area with the originating transaction ID and program name recorded.
